description:
PROBLEM
Prompt-injection boundary markers are not yet explicit around artifact bodies that later flow into prompt assembly. The current server-side artifact readers in `cli/internal/server/state_executions.go:205-217` clamp text for transport, but they do not wrap the body in an explicit untrusted-data envelope for downstream prompt renderers. The review prompt path in `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1561-1630` only uses XML tags for the bead envelope; it does not mark artifact content with a dedicated boundary contract.

ROOT CAUSE
There is no shared delimiter helper for untrusted artifact bodies. The current prompt builders rely on ad hoc XML wrappers and transport clamping, which are not the same thing as a prompt-injection boundary that clearly distinguishes trusted instructions from untrusted artifact text.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a small helper (likely in `cli/internal/evidence` or the prompt-rendering package that owns the assembler) that wraps artifact bodies in a canonical untrusted-data delimiter pair.
- Update the prompt-rendering call sites that inline artifact bodies to use the wrapper before interpolation.
- Add a regression test named `TestArtifactBodyDelimitedAsUntrusted` that asserts the delimiter pair appears around the artifact payload and that the raw body is still preserved inside the wrapper.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not alter the transport-level clamp behavior or its `truncated` metadata.
- Do not change review verdict parsing or the FEAT-022 telemetry schema in this slice.
- Do not rewrite unrelated server text egress paths.

description:
PROBLEM
The normal `internal/agent` race gate invokes production host-wide process discovery from default worker-loop fixtures. On Niflheim this produced multi-gigabyte Go test cache output, five concurrent provider-launch helpers, rising cgroup file/slab memory, and validation times long enough to prevent otherwise small reliability fixes from landing. The initial three-child split separated the scanner seam from fixture migration, but each intermediate bead must independently pass `lefthook run pre-commit`; a seam-only commit leaves the full package gate non-hermetic, while migration cannot compile before the seam lands. This child therefore owns the smallest independently green atomic slice: seam plus default-fixture migration plus production-coverage proof.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1685-1700` unconditionally constructs `newOrphanHarnessProcessScanner()` during worker startup.
- `cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper_linux.go:22-66` enumerates every `/proc` PID and reads cmdline, cwd, and stat.
- Default worker-loop fixtures including `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_priority_test.go:87-188` and `TestExecuteBeadWorkerEndToEndThreeBeadDrain` enter that production startup path even though they test queue behavior, not orphan recovery.
- Linux recovery tests such as `TestWorkStartupReaper_KillsOrphanProcessGroup` are the intentional production-scanner coverage and must remain real.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an explicit worker-loop/orphan-reaper scanner seam whose nil/default preserves production behavior. Add a shared bounded fake/no-op scanner helper for tests and inject it into every default worker-loop fixture that is not testing orphan discovery/recovery, including the two named queue fixtures. Keep the Linux orphan-reaper tests on the production scanner. Add a tripwire that fails if those default fixtures fall through to host `/proc` discovery. Land these changes together so the staged package-wide hook is green in this attempt.

NON-SCOPE
Changing production orphan ownership or reaping policy, weakening Linux real-process integration coverage, changing queue ordering, changing provider routing, or skipping the mandatory package-wide hook.

PARENT
`ddx-393abd29`. This child supersedes the original seam-only intermediate scope because that split could not satisfy its own full-gate acceptance independently.

DEPS
None. Later children `ddx-d9caa6fc` and `ddx-5011e1a8` remain as already-satisfied verification closures after this atomic slice lands.
notes:
Expanded from seam-only to the atomic independently-green slice on 2026-07-13 after live validation proved the original seam→fixture dependency split could not pass the mandatory package-wide hook at either intermediate commit.

After the green tool returned, the routed Codex harness made no further tool call for more than ten minutes; the operator checkpointed the clean diff and terminated only model PGID 1968095. DDx recorded result_rev c6dd2b61b and transport termination. Recover that checkpoint instead of reimplementing it, reuse the durable green gate evidence, and do not launch an unchanged second package run.

description:
PROBLEM
Run record updates for running and terminal phases must never leave partial JSON if the process is interrupted. Without an explicit interruption test around these update paths, a killed worker could corrupt .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json and make run state unreadable.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:230-233 calls FizeauService.Execute and then consumes public execution events, while cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:295-317 and cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:465-490 still synthesize run-layer state from sessions and bundles when no stored record exists. The Phase 3 WB-2 plan at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149 requires the DDx-owned record to transition through running and terminal states using atomic updates so readers see either the prior valid record or the next complete record.

PROPOSED FIX
Add focused interruption coverage around the run-record writer/update path used for running and terminal transitions. Inject failure or kill timing during each update and verify .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json remains valid JSON representing either the prior complete record or the next complete record. Reuse the existing schema/writer abstraction rather than adding a separate persistence mechanism.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route, add new outcome semantics, or change the public Fizeau route/result contract.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
Original bead ddx-61c41896. Queue parent field ddx-5bf0f8d0.

DEPS
Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit. Requires the run-record schema/writer and pre-dispatch publish children to be available before final wiring.

description:
PROBLEM
The live execute-bead path does not supply gate or implementation-command evidence to its integrity validator, and its prompts do not explicitly prohibit hook bypass. A provider can therefore run git commit --no-verify after a required gate fails or is interrupted and still reach merge/close.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1507-1514 invokes ValidateAttemptIntegrity without GateRuns or implementation-command evidence. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2108-2113 and 2143-2148 ask for tests and lefthook but do not forbid --no-verify, hook disabling, or committing after a failed or interrupted required gate.

PROPOSED FIX
Capture foreground gate commands, outputs, exit status, ordering relative to the final staged mutation and implementation commit, plus implementation-agent git commands from the harness session. Pass that evidence to ValidateAttemptIntegrity before landing. Preserve an invalid attempt with failure_mode=attempt_integrity. Update every rich and embedded execute-bead prompt to forbid --no-verify, hook disabling, and committing after required-gate failure or interruption.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go
- nearest harness-session evidence adapter
- execute-bead prompt builders and snapshot tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not redesign the pure validation policy owned by ddx-c4497391. Do not rewrite existing execution history or forbid DDx-owned checkpoint, tracker-only, landing, or durable-audit commits.

PARENT
ddx-9c3e703b.

DEPS
ddx-c4497391.

description:
PROBLEM
When ddx work parks a bead for operator attention after a no_evidence_produced outcome, the needs-human-summary and needs-human-suggested-action custom fields always read "attempt produced dirty rescue but no landed evidence" / "inspect the dirty rescue patch, commit valid work manually, then move the bead back to open if another automated attempt is needed" — even when the attempt was a plain no-commit exit with no dirty rescue at all. Observed live on ddx-1bc702ec: today's park (2026-07-25T21:33:02) recorded result.json outcome "no_evidence_produced" with reason "agent exited without a commit or no_changes_rationale.txt" (no PreserveRef, no NoEvidencePaths), yet `ddx bead show ddx-1bc702ec` displays the dirty-rescue narrative verbatim, identical to an unrelated dirty-rescue incident from 2026-07-18. Operators reading needs-human-summary get a categorically wrong diagnosis and a suggested action (inspect a dirty patch) that does not apply, defeating the purpose of the operator-attention gate.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3935-3954 computes a correct, per-attempt detail string (`detail := strings.TrimSpace(firstNonEmpty(report.Detail, report.Error))`, defaulting to "agent exited without a commit or no_changes_rationale.txt") and passes it to parkNoEvidenceForOperator, but that detail is only threaded into the JSON body of the operator_attention event (line 6772: `"detail": detail`).
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6754-6767 (parkNoEvidenceForOperator) hardcodes Summary and SuggestedAction as compile-time-constant strings describing a dirty-rescue scenario, unconditionally, regardless of whether report.PreserveRef or report.NoEvidencePaths are actually set. Only Reason (line 6756-6758) is conditioned on the dirty-rescue check; Summary (line 6761) and SuggestedAction (line 6762) are not, so a plain no-evidence park always gets the dirty-rescue narrative.
cli/internal/bead/reconcile.go:56-65 (SetNeedsHumanMeta) writes all five needs-human-* fields atomically from whatever Summary/SuggestedAction it's given — the write mechanism itself is not at fault; it faithfully persists the wrong, hardcoded input it receives.

PROPOSED FIX
In parkNoEvidenceForOperator, derive distinct Summary/SuggestedAction text for the two cases already distinguished by the existing reason variable (dirty rescue vs. plain no-evidence), using the detail parameter (or report.Detail/report.Error) for the plain case instead of the hardcoded dirty-rescue strings. Preserve the current dirty-rescue text only for the branch where report.PreserveRef or report.NoEvidencePaths is actually set.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change SetNeedsHumanMeta's write mechanism (internal/bead/reconcile.go:56-65) — it already writes all five fields correctly in lockstep. Do not change parkToProposedWithOperatorMeta or parkToProposedWithIntakeMeta. Do not alter the ParkReason/reason classification logic beyond reading its existing result. Do not touch the dirty-rescue code path's own diagnostic text.

acceptance:
1. `Store.Claim` refuses to claim a bead with an unclosed blocking dependency, returning an error satisfying `errors.Is(err, ErrDependencyGateRejected)` naming the open dep ID, leaving status unchanged (still open, no lease written). Covered by `TestClaim_RefusesBlockedBead` in cli/internal/bead/store_test.go.
2. `Store.ClaimWithOptions` refuses the same case with the same wrapped error and writes no lease; covered by `TestClaimWithOptions_RefusesBlockedBead`.
3. Claiming a bead whose blocking deps are all closed still succeeds (no regression); covered by an assertion in `TestClaim_RefusesBlockedBead` or a sibling `TestClaim_AllowsReadyBead`.
4. `cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/... green`.
5. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM: A dependency-blocked bead can be claimed directly, because claim checks only lifecycle status and lease staleness, not dependency readiness. A worker or operator can begin work on a bead whose prerequisite is still open — the precondition that leads to premature/unsafe closes.

ROOT CAUSE: `Store.Claim` (cli/internal/bead/store.go:955) and `Store.ClaimWithOptions` (store.go:1026) validate only `beads[i].Status` (StatusOpen / stalled StatusInProgress) and `claimLeaseIsStale` (store.go:968,973), then transition to StatusInProgress via `transitionLifecycleInPlace` (store.go:980). Dependency-waiting is a derived queue bucket (`Blocked`, store.go:2663; classifier store.go:2287) — a dep-blocked bead's persisted status is still `open`, so neither method rejects it. The `ddx work` ready-queue (`ReadyExecution`, store.go:2445) already excludes dep-waiting beads, but direct `Store.Claim` calls (e.g. `ddx bead update --claim` at cmd/bead.go:774) have no such guard. Confirmed: no dependency check exists on the claim path.

PROPOSED FIX: Depends on the sibling bead adding `Store.UnclosedBlockingDeps(id)` and `ErrDependencyGateRejected` (cli/internal/bead/errors.go, store.go). In both `Store.Claim` and `Store.ClaimWithOptions`, inside the `WithLock` block after locating the target bead and before the transition/lease write, call `s.UnclosedBlockingDeps(id)`; if it returns a non-empty slice, return `fmt.Errorf("%w: cannot claim %s: %s", ErrDependencyGateRejected, id, strings.Join(open, ", "))` without mutating the bead or writing a lease. This is defense-in-depth behind the ready-queue filter for callers that claim by ID directly. If the sibling primitive has not landed, add a minimal locked-context resolver inline at these two call sites.

NON-SCOPE: Do NOT change close/roll-up paths (sibling beads). Do NOT change lease staleness / heartbeat logic (`claimLeaseIsStale` store.go:1090, `writeClaimHeartbeat` claim_liveness.go:185). Do NOT change the ready-queue classifier or `ddx work` drain ordering. Do NOT gate stalled-reclaim differently — the same dep gate applies uniformly to open and stalled-reclaim entry.

description:
PROBLEM (Principle 1 of epic ddx-602ae31a)

Eliminate hardcoded .ddx/ paths so that DDx state anchors correctly regardless of whether the project has a .ddx/ folder. Today every code path joins filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...) directly, so introducing an XDG fallback or any other root strategy means a many-callsite rewrite.

DESIGN

ddxroot.Path(ctx, projectRoot) is the single accessor. It returns:
- <projectRoot>/.ddx — when that directory exists (in-tree mode)
- ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ — otherwise (convention mode)

Project identity in convention mode is parsed from `git remote get-url origin`:
- https://github.com/easel/ddx.git → github.com/easel/ddx
- git@github.com:easel/ddx.git → github.com/easel/ddx
- https://gitlab.example.com/team/repo → gitlab.example.com/team/repo
- Local (no remote) → local/<basename>-<short-hash-of-abs-path>

The XDG project directory IS a git repository — `git init`ed on first bootstrap. All DDx state for that project (beads.jsonl, attachments, archive, plugins, etc.) lives there and is versioned. Operators can `git remote add` it to a server to share state with teammates.

WORKTREE REGISTRY (required, not speculative)

Each XDG project root maintains <xdg>/worktrees.json:

  {"paths": [{"path": "/Users/erik/Projects/ddx", "first_seen_at": "...", "last_seen_at": "...", "hostname": "..."}], "master": "/Users/erik/Projects/ddx"}

- The first worktree to bootstrap an XDG project is auto-marked master.
- Subsequent worktrees register as non-master.
- `ddx project worktree list` shows the registry.
- `ddx project worktree master <path>` re-pins.
- Audit log entries (bead events with result_rev/base_rev) include the master path so downstream tools resolve commit SHAs to a known worktree.

DDX_ROOT NEVER PUNNED — bootstrap is atomic, idempotent, and a no-op when the directory already exists. Two concurrent ddx invocations on the same project must not race-create or race-write worktrees.json. Use file-locking (existing gitlock pattern from ddx-6a518fd9) where needed.

AUDIT — every Go file in cli/ that contains the literal ".ddx" as a path segment must route through ddxroot.Path. Touched packages at minimum:
- cli/cmd/ (every command that reads/writes state)
- cli/internal/agent/ (execute_bead*, work/, escalation/)
- cli/internal/bead/ (store, migrate, lifecycle)
- cli/internal/server/ (workers, federation, GraphQL adapters)
- cli/internal/config/ (resolved, types)
- cli/internal/triage/, cli/internal/metaprompt/, cli/internal/registry/
- library/checks/ (where ddx-side paths exist)

A regression linter (lefthook hook or go vet analyzer) blocks any PR that introduces a new filepath.Join(..., ".ddx", ...) literal outside cli/internal/ddxroot/.

SPEC IMPACT — the following docs reference .ddx/ paths and must be updated in this bead:
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md (state paths)
- docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-019-multi-project-server-topology.md (project identity)
- docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-020-multi-machine-coordinator-topology.md (project identity)
- docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-021-operator-prompt-beads-web-write-path.md (operator-prompt paths)
- docs/helix/02-design/workers-sessions-operator-surface.md (worker status paths)
- docs/helix/02-design/plan-2026-04-29-artifact-and-run-architecture.md (FEAT-010 runs/)

Each spec update: replace .ddx/<path> citations with ddxroot.Path()/<path> AND add a "project identity" subsection where applicable referencing this bead.

NON-SCOPE
- Skills/personas install strategy (principle 2 — separate bead).
- Test matrix (separate bead).
- Migrating today's in-tree ddx-repo to convention mode (out of scope; this repo stays in-tree as the dogfooding canon).

DEPS
None. This is the foundational refactor.

description:
PROBLEM
  Story 14 requires federated query resolvers that aggregate beads, runs, and projects across registered spokes. Today the GraphQL schema at cli/internal/server/graphql/schema.graphql defines FederatedBead, FederatedRun, and FederatedProject types and the corresponding query fields, but write-routing (hub forwards mutations to owning spoke) is not implemented, and the resolver_federation.go file has no mutation forwarding.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_federation.go:61 defines FederatedBeads, :124 defines FederatedRuns, and :184 defines FederatedProjects — all read-only fan-out via FederationProvider.FanOut (cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_federation.go:31). cli/internal/federation/fanout.go:208 provides the FanOutClient.Execute fan-out transport. No mutation resolver in resolver_mutation_*.go calls FanOut or routes writes to an owning spoke; mutations remain hub-local. The ownerSpoke routing metadata fields (nodeID, spokeURL) are populated by existing fan-out code but no write-routing contract enforces "hub forwards, never broadcasts."

PROPOSED FIX
  - Add write-routing helper in cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_federation.go: routeToOwner(ctx, ownerSpokeURL, mutationQuery, variables) error that forwards mutations via HTTP to the owning spoke.
  - Wire routeToOwner into the relevant mutation resolvers in resolver_mutation_beads.go or resolver_mutation_runs.go for any mutation that operates on a federated resource.
  - Add schema.graphql comment block documenting the write-routing contract ("hub forwards to ownerSpoke; never broadcasts").
  - Name the ownerSpoke field on FederatedBead/FederatedRun/FederatedProject as the routing discriminator.

NON-SCOPE
  - New non-federated resolvers (covered by Story 13).
  - Spoke discovery and registration (covered by ddx-fe63969f).
  - Federated mutations on FederatedProject (out of Story 14 scope; read-only for projects).

description:
PROBLEM
While the managed DDx worker decomposed ddx-29491a0e on 2026-07-13, the preclaim-decompose Codex provider remained live for more than two minutes, but `ddx work status --json` changed to active_work.count=0 and reported no bead_id, phase, or last_activity_at. After the decomposer returned, an interactive nested `codex --no-alt-screen` process (PID 607041, process group 607041) remained directly under the DDx worker until the operator terminated it. Operators therefore see an apparently idle worker while queue-critical model work is running and preclaim providers can leak CPU after successful fallback.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 constructs the sidecar liveness reporter but explicitly defers emission until a bead is claimed. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without setting a resolving phase, ticking liveness, or wrapping the hook in provider-descendant cleanup. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:16 and :59-74 give this preclaim operation a separate fixed eight-minute timeout, so it bypasses the configured five-minute preclaim bound from cli/internal/agent/work/guard.go:15 and :95-99. Attempt-end descendant reaping in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1150-1163 is never reached because decomposition happens before an implementation attempt exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Publish candidate-scoped resolving liveness before dispatching preclaim decomposition, heartbeat it while the provider runs, and include provider-child observations without creating a bead lease. Bound the call by the configured preclaim timeout supplied to the execute loop rather than a longer hard-coded timeout. Establish a preclaim lifecycle process baseline and reap every provider descendant introduced by the hook on success, deterministic fallback, error, timeout, and cancellation. Clear transient resolving state on every exit and preserve the existing loop.start event ordering contract.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
None; root reliability regression.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:
PROBLEM
The watchdog reaper still mirrors the Stop path's pid-limited cleanup. A stalled managed worker can be marked reaped and have its bead claim released, yet still leave descendants behind unless reap uses the same managed-tree cleanup path as Stop.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1347-1414 selects reaping candidates and passes only pid into reapWorker.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1417-1482 emits bead.reaped, releases the bead claim, and then calls terminateProcessGroup(pid, grace) only when pid > 0.
cli/internal/server/workers.go:1453-1457 shows the same pid-only limitation that exists in Stop, but the reap path is separate and can drift if it does not reuse the shared cleanup helper.

PROPOSED FIX
- Route watchdog reaping through the same managed-worker tree cleanup helper used by Stop.
- Keep bead.reaped emission, claim release, and terminal-state persistence intact.
- Make the reap path idempotent so repeated sweeps do not double-clean the same worker.
- Add a process-tree test that proves watchdog reap follows the SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL path and releases the claimed bead.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not add restart policy logic in this bead.
- Do not change Stop beyond the shared helper reuse already required by the stop bead.
- Do not touch external workers or CLI commands.

ACCEPTANCE
1. TestManagedWorkerWatchdogReapKillsProcessTree proves watchdog reap follows the same SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL cleanup path and releases the claimed bead.
2. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... -run "TestManagedWorkerWatchdogReapKillsProcessTree" passes.
3. make install is run after the code change lands.
4. lefthook run pre-commit passes.

description:
# PROBLEM
`*Store` exposes 7 migration-tooling methods used by `cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go` and related admin commands: `MigrateLifecycle`, `MigrateFromHelix`, `MigrateToAxon`, `MigrateDryRun`, `MigrateLifecycleDryRun`, `DetectLifecycleMigrationRequired`, `ReconcileLifecycleMetadata`. These are admin/one-shot tooling, not steady-state Backend operations. After the BL bead moves concrete `*Store` to `cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/`, `cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go` cannot reach these methods. They need an exposure path that doesn't violate the boundary lockdown.

# ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/bead/store.go` exposes the 7 migration methods. `cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go` imports `cli/internal/bead` and calls them on `*Store` concretely. Per TD-027 §11.5 + Migration row in the mutation rules table, these are admin tools not on the `Backend` interface. After BL, the only public surface in `cli/internal/bead/` is what's exported there — concrete `*Store` won't be reachable.

# PROPOSED FIX

Per the converged design recommendation (separate factory rather than `BeadMigration` sub-interface on Backend, to avoid forcing every backend to stub source-specific migrations):

1. Create `cli/internal/bead/migrator.go` with a `Migrator` interface and `NewMigrator` factory:
   ```go
   type Migrator interface {
       MigrateLifecycle(ctx context.Context, opts MigrationOptions) (MigrationResult, error)
       MigrateLifecycleDryRun(ctx context.Context, opts MigrationOptions) (MigrationResult, error)
       MigrateFromHelix(ctx context.Context, src string) error
       MigrateToAxon(ctx context.Context, opts MigrateToAxonOptions) error  // deprecated; replaced by ddx-IMP
       MigrateDryRun(ctx context.Context, opts MigrationOptions) (MigrationResult, error)
       DetectLifecycleMigrationRequired(ctx context.Context) (bool, MigrationReport, error)
       ReconcileLifecycleMetadata(ctx context.Context) (ReconcileReport, error)
   }
   ```

2. Move the 7 methods' bodies from `*Store` (in `cli/internal/bead/store.go` and `migrate.go`) onto an unexported `*storeMigrator` type that holds a `*Store` reference and implements `Migrator`. The `NewMigrator` factory returns this.

3. Update `cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go` and any related admin commands:

4. Remove `*Store.MigrateLifecycle`, `MigrateLifecycleDryRun`, `MigrateFromHelix`, `MigrateToAxon`, `MigrateDryRun`, `DetectLifecycleMigrationRequired`, `ReconcileLifecycleMetadata` from the `*Store` public method set. Logic moves to the `*storeMigrator` type.

- Schema-versioning migration ladder framework — deferred until first breaking change is proposed.

description:
PROBLEM
Runtime artifact validation must inspect Complete/Implemented document fixtures without rewriting status stamps, Verification mapping rows, or evidence target text. If analyzer execution restamps or normalizes documents during linting, the lint is unsafe to run in pre-commit and can hide stale or invalid evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no document-level no-mutation check around runtime-artifact validation for parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Add analyzer-level coverage that runs spechonesty over Complete/Implemented document fixtures using the parsed Verification rows and runtime artifact resolver. The test should assert diagnostics are emitted in memory and the document fixture bytes remain unchanged, specifically protecting status stamps, mapping rows, and evidence target text from rewrite/restamp behavior.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change diagnostic content beyond what is required to exercise read-only validation. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that. Do not add generic fixture mutation coverage in this bead; that is covered by the sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
  The heartbeat goroutine in the drain loop is inlined, coupling ticker lifecycle management with candidate execution and blocking unit tests from verifying heartbeat behavior without a real ticker.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:732-753 inlines a goroutine + sync.WaitGroup + time.NewTicker(heartbeatInterval) directly in the loop body. hbCtx and hbWG are declared locally; the goroutine calls w.Store.Heartbeat(beadID) on every tick. There is no injection seam, so tests cannot stub the ticker to verify heartbeat cadence or cancellation without real wall-clock delays.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Extract to withHeartbeat(ctx context.Context, beadID string, interval time.Duration, store interface{ Heartbeat(string) error }, fn func() (ExecuteBeadReport, error)) error in a new file cli/internal/agent/work/heartbeat.go.
  - withHeartbeat starts the internal goroutine + WaitGroup, calls fn(), cancels the ticker goroutine on fn return, and returns fn's result.
  - Drain loop body (execute_bead_loop.go:732) replaces the inline goroutine block with a single withHeartbeat call.
  - Add TestWithHeartbeat_TickerFiredBeforeReturn and TestWithHeartbeat_CancelPropagates to cli/internal/agent/work/heartbeat_test.go using a stub ticker channel injection.

NON-SCOPE
  - File renames (C13, ddx-387a0178).
  - Changes to heartbeatInterval policy or the Store.Heartbeat call itself.
  - Any behavior change to the drain loop; this is a pure extraction.

INTERSECTIONS
- P2: heartbeat timing and lifecycle belong in one helper, not inline with candidate execution.
- P4: one bead heartbeat bug must not leak into the rest of the drain loop.
- P5: extracted heartbeat behavior supports always-visible worker state.

After the CLI removes top-level `ddx install`, active docs and bundled skills must stop instructing users or agents to run `ddx install helix`, `ddx install ddx --force`, `ddx installed`, or `ddx uninstall` for skill/plugin distribution. Current skill guidance has already started moving toward marketplace install, but installed and source copies can drift, and active website/docs/help snippets still contain old install examples.

ROOT CAUSE

description:
PROBLEM
  The run/try/work dispatch paths must not set Profile, Harness, or Model directly on ResolvedConfig or Runtime structs — those are durable knobs that belong in config.LoadAndResolve. Without a mechanically-enforced lint rule, future edits can silently reintroduce the anti-pattern and bypass the fizeau routing contract.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/tools/lint/routinglint/analyzer.go (package routinglint) currently forbids retired compensating-routing identifiers (ResolveProfileLadder, ResolveTierModelRef, etc.) and flag literals (--escalate, profile_ladders). It does not yet forbid direct field assignment of Profile/Harness/Model on Runtime structs inside run/try/work command code paths. The SD-024 runtimelint analyzer (cli/tools/lint/runtimelint/analyzer.go:41) forbids durable-knob fields on *Runtime structs generically, but does not name a per-command allowlist or produce a test that verifies the run/work/try paths specifically. No TestRoutingLint* test exercises this invariant.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Extend routinglint (cli/tools/lint/routinglint/analyzer.go) to flag direct Profile/Harness/Model field assignment on types matching *Runtime in cli/cmd/ run/work/try command files, or add a new rule in runtimelint covering this.
  - Alternatively, add a targeted integration test TestRoutingLint_RunPathNeverSetsProfileDirectly that runs the analyzer against the live tree and asserts zero diagnostics for the assignment pattern.
  - Fix any existing violations: cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1893-1897 passes overrides.Profile/Harness/Model through CLIOverrides to config.LoadAndResolve — verify this is compliant (CLIOverrides is not a Runtime struct).

NON-SCOPE
  - Changes to agent_run or agent_run_overrides command behavior.
  - Changes to the fizeau or ladder routing logic.
  - Lint rules for non-routing fields on Runtime structs (covered by runtimelint).

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still exposes top-level install commands even though agent-facing skill distribution should move to the marketplace installer. `cli/cmd/command_factory.go:627-629` registers `newInstallCommand`, `newInstalledCommand`, and `newUninstallCommand`. `cli/cmd/install.go:22-90` begins the public `ddx install` implementation, and the rest of that file contains public installed/uninstall command implementations plus helper code. The user explicitly asked to remove the `ddx install` code.

ROOT CAUSE
The install command surface predates the marketplace-plugin direction. It now competes with `npx claude-plugins install ...` and keeps encouraging DDx-owned skill/package install behavior.

PROPOSED FIX
- Audit direct references to `newInstallCommand`, `newInstalledCommand`, `newUninstallCommand`, `runInstall`, `runInstalled`, and `runUninstall` before deletion.
- Remove top-level command registration from `cli/cmd/command_factory.go:627-629`.
- Delete or shrink `cli/cmd/install.go` so removed public command code no longer builds into DDx. Preserve registry/internal helpers only if a concrete caller still needs them; move retained helpers to a non-command file with names that do not imply top-level install UX.
- Update command-surface/help tests so `ddx install`, `ddx installed`, and `ddx uninstall` are not listed and return unknown-command errors.
- Remove obsolete install/global tests that exclusively assert removed command behavior. Preserve tests for retained internal registry/manifest behavior by moving them to registry/plugin tests where appropriate.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove the lower-level registry package if `init`, `update`, `persona`, `plugin`, or embedded default resolution still uses it.
- Do not remove `ddx plugin` in this bead unless the dependency audit proves it is only an alias for deleted install commands.
- Do not implement marketplace installation inside DDx.

DEPS
Depends on ddx-39b8b2fd so doctor has the new marketplace remediation before the old command disappears.

acceptance:
1. TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagRunsWorkLoop proves the hidden ddx work --server-managed <worker-id> entry point reads the persisted spec and runs the same execute-loop path used by current server-managed workers.
2. TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagRejectsMissingSpec proves the entry point exits with an actionable error when the worker ID has no persisted ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec.
3. TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagUsesPersistedSpec proves the entry point uses the persisted worker spec instead of reconstructing execution parameters from defaults.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... ./cmd/... -run 'TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagRunsWorkLoop|TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagRejectsMissingSpec|TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagUsesPersistedSpec' passes.
5. make install is run after the code change lands.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
StartExecuteLoop needs a subprocess target that runs the same execute-loop behavior as current server-managed workers. Without a hidden server-managed entry point, the server can spawn a process group but cannot hand that process the persisted ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec and have it perform the drain loop.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:192 defines WorkerManager as managing in-process work workers as goroutines. cli/internal/server/workers.go:438-462 directly calls drainProgress and runWorker rather than invoking a process entry point. The CLI command surface for ddx work currently has no hidden --server-managed <worker-id> path that reads the persisted worker spec and enters the existing execute-loop path.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a hidden ddx work --server-managed <worker-id> entry point, or an equivalent hidden internal entry point, that reads the persisted ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec for the worker ID and runs the same execute-loop path used by current server-managed workers. Reuse existing WorkerManager/runWorker behavior where possible so claim, execution, progress, and reaping behavior do not fork into a parallel implementation. Ensure the parent server launch path can pass only the worker ID and rely on persisted spec state.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement process-group PID/PGID persistence beyond what is needed to call the entry point; that is covered by a sibling child bead. Do not kill external reported workers or interactive Claude/Codex sessions. Do not change bead claim semantics except releasing claims for the stopped/reaped managed worker. Do not implement UI controls.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT AND RELATIONSHIP
Parent bead: ddx-24a3da84. Original parent relationship cited by the too-large bead: ddx-9d1af129. Governing artifact reference: plan:server-managed-workers. No explicit dependency IDs were provided by the parent bead.

title: server: add server-managed work loop entry point
work-last-detail: Claude TUI PTY closed before Stop hook; process exit code 1

acceptance:
1. Add `TestExecutionCleanupManager_ApplyReapsOnlyStaleAttemptProcessGroups` using injected scanner/killer fakes where needed, proving `--apply` terminates only stale DDx-owned attempt process groups.
2. Add `TestExecutionCleanupManager_ApplyPreservesLiveAndForeignProcessGroups` proving live run-state, live worker sidecar, active registered worktree, other-project processes, and uncertain candidates are preserved with operator-visible warnings when appropriate.
3. Add `TestExecutionCleanupManager_ApplyTerminatesGracefullyThenBoundedKill` or an equivalent assertion proving the killer uses graceful terminate before bounded kill when a process group remains alive.
4. Existing process-reaper tests remain green: `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'OrphanHarness|Executor|DockerCloneBackend_ProcessGroupCleanup' -count=1` passes.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'ExecutionCleanupManager_Apply.*Process|ProcessReap|AttemptDescendant|OrphanHarness|Executor|DockerCloneBackend_ProcessGroupCleanup' -count=1` passes.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
`ddx cleanup --apply` can delete stale DDx execution files, but it cannot terminate stale DDx-owned attempt-descendant process groups that are provably orphaned. Heavy leftover processes can continue burning CPU or holding ports after their original attempt is gone.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:230-527` applies file cleanup for stale temp dirs, worktrees, scratch roots, stale run-state files, evidence dirs, logs, worker dirs, and refs, but contains no safe process-group termination path.
- `cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:110-138` has no process reaping counts or warnings in `ExecutionCleanupSummary`, so apply mode cannot report terminated, preserved, blocked, or unsafe process groups.
- `cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:82-100` and `cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:155-168` intentionally gate startup harness reaping on top-level harness names and dead bead lease owners; that does not cover descendant process groups whose harness root has already exited.
- `cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:10-29` sets process group and parent-death attributes for normal harness children, which cleanup can use only when stale ownership and liveness evidence prove the group is DDx-owned and safe to reap.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend execution cleanup apply mode with an injectable process-group killer and conservative stale ownership checks. Apply may terminate only process groups associated with the current project's DDx execution root where run-state cleanup liveness is expired or missing, the recorded owner PID is gone, the worktree is under the current project execution root, and no live worker sidecar or active registered worktree owns it. Preserve live run-state, live worker sidecar, active registered worktree, other-project processes, and any uncertain candidate. Prefer graceful terminate followed by bounded kill where feasible. Surface blocked warnings instead of silently deleting files when a process is detected but cannot be killed safely.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- `cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go` and adjacent new platform-specific process cleanup files/tests.
- `cli/internal/workerstatus/*` or `cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper*` only for reused process-scanning helpers, not broad rewrites.
- `docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-010-task-execution.md` and `docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-025-task-execution-lifecycle.md` only if this child changes the documented cleanup contract.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not edit Niflheim.
- Do not duplicate `ddx-e0de6369`; that bead owns `.ddx/harness-sessions/` scratch ignore/prune behavior.
- Do not duplicate `ddx-bbea954f`; that bead owns dirty timeout worktree edit preservation before cleanup deletion.
- Do not replace the existing parent-death/process-group fixes from `ddx-0d7d5f0e`, `ddx-3113d524`, or `ddx-418c3849`.
- Do not implement a general-purpose port scanner or host process manager. Port conflict recovery here comes only from safely reaping stale DDx-owned attempt process groups.
- Do not kill processes outside the current project's DDx execution root, processes tied to live run-state/worker liveness, active registered worktrees, or non-DDx user workloads.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
- `spec:FEAT-010`
- `spec:SD-025`

description:
PROBLEM
DDx workers need to publish .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json durably before dispatch, but there is no crash-safe writer. A partial or torn JSON record would make the run substrate unreliable for workers, CLI readers, and later server read-path work.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:15-55 only reads legacy server-private run projections and does not provide a writer. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149 requires atomic write-fsync-rename discipline for .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json. There is no writer package in cli/internal/agent that writes temp files, fsyncs the file, renames into place, and fsyncs the parent directory.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an atomic publish helper under cli/internal/agent for v1 run records. The helper should write to a temp file in the target directory, fsync the file after JSON encoding, rename it over record.json, and fsync the parent directory. It should leave either the previous complete record or the next complete record visible after interruption. Keep the helper package-private or narrowly scoped unless existing agent package patterns require an exported API.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route, add CLI runs list/show verbs, repoint GraphQL read paths, migrate .ddx/exec/runs, .ddx/exec-runs, or .ddx/executions, implement recovery transitions, or change retention policy. Do not introduce a general-purpose BlobStore; FEAT-028 remains deferred.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
ddx-61c41896. Upstream parent field from original bead: ddx-5bf0f8d0.

Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit.

1. `ddx init --global --silent` exits 0 and creates ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx/ with the bundled library content.
2. `ddx init --global` is idempotent: running twice does not error and does not destroy local-only files under global/.
3. TestInitGlobal_PopulatesXDGGlobalDir asserts the directory structure post-install matches what convention mode expects.
4. TestInitGlobal_IsIdempotent asserts a second run does not error and re-syncs the plugin content.
5. TestConventionMode_ReadsGlobalSkillsBeforeHardcoded asserts that with --global installed, convention mode picks up the global plugin instead of the hardcoded one.
6. ddx doctor's "Global Install" check exists and reports the install path + status.
7. cd cli && go test ./cmd/... ./internal/config/... green.
8. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Convention mode (per ddx-ad338ec3) bootstraps an XDG project dir but has no source for skills, personas, or the default ddx plugin. Either every project re-downloads the plugin on first use, or the user must have a global install. The latter is the better answer: install once per machine, all convention-mode projects share.

ROOT CAUSE
There is no per-user install path today. `ddx init` only writes per-project state. Skills/personas live in the project's .ddx/plugins/ (in-tree) or are missing entirely (convention).

PROPOSED FIX

1. Add `ddx init --global` flag (and corresponding code path in cli/cmd/init.go). When set:
   - Resolve target path: ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/ (defaults to ~/.local/share/ddx/global/).
   - Install the default ddx plugin (library/ contents) into ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/plugins/ddx/.
   - Write a default ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml with convention defaults (library URL, branch, etc.).
   - Idempotent: re-running upgrades to a newer plugin version but does not destroy operator state.

2. Convention mode reads ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/ as the second precedence tier (in-tree > global > hardcoded). If --global has never been run, fall back to baked-in hardcoded defaults — convention mode still works without it; --global is an optimization for users who want offline-cacheable plugin content.

3. Document the install path in ddx doctor: a new check "Global Install" reports whether ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/ exists and points operators to `ddx init --global` if it does not.

4. Do NOT remove the existing per-project plugin install (in-tree mode at .ddx/plugins/<name>/). Both coexist.

NON-SCOPE
- In-project ddx init manifest write (E4 bead).
- Migration from legacy ~/.config/ddx/ or ~/.ddx/ if such exist on disk (none expected; today there is no global install).
- Plugin update / upgrade flow for the global install (use existing `ddx update` mechanism; verify it works against the new path).

DEPS
ddx-564ea1cf (E1) — resolver must exist.
ddx-ad338ec3 (E2) — convention mode reads from this path.
notes: Superseded by epic restructure into 3 consolidated beads aligned to the two principles: (1) bulletproof ddx home resolution, (2) centralized vs in-project skills/personas. New beads pending.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx-359e812b` is still too broad for what remains. `docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-002-server-web-ui.md:340-351,353-363` keeps bead, spec, and document writes planned, but the current Playwright suite already covers the mocked forwarded paths in `cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/beads-queue-mutations.spec.ts:210-268` and `cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/spec-editing.spec.ts:204-256`, while `cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/federation-2node.spec.ts:219-307` already covers the read-federation shell around the owner-write entry points.

ROOT CAUSE
The stale bead conflates three concerns: hub/spoke federation reads, mocked UI write-forwarding, and the live owner-targeted persistence gap. FEAT-026 says forwarding is owner-targeted and never broadcast (`docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-026-federation.md:22-29,160-177`), so the bead should only track the missing live bead/document write persistence and refusal behavior, not the already-covered smoke paths.

PROPOSED FIX
- Rewrite or supersede `ddx-359e812b` so it narrows to live owner-targeted bead create/edit and documentWrite persistence.
- Keep the ts-net guard as a separate child if it is still load-bearing.
- Add or update the missing owner-write tests as `TestFederatedBeadWrite_ForwardsToOwner`, `TestFederatedDocumentWrite_ForwardsToOwner`, `TestFederatedWrite_RejectsOfflineSpoke`, and `TestFederatedWrite_IdempotentRequestID`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not add new federation read smoke.
- Do not add screenshot assertions.
- Do not implement managed-node outbound control from ADR-028.
- Do not change the mocked Playwright smoke paths unless they are being split out of this bead.

PARENT + DEPS
Parent: `ddx-a038a090`. Upstream stale bead context: `ddx-28f3cf37`.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still infers price, billing category, subscription status, display identity, and evidence limits from concrete model/harness/provider names. These facts become stale as Fizeau changes routes and cause unknown cost to be presented as an estimate or fabricated paid/subscription/local category. Concrete route identity also changes prompt-size policy through per-harness evidence caps.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/pricing.go:3-34 contains a DDx model-price table and EstimateCost.

acceptance:
1. TestSupervisorReconcile_LiveDiskOnlyAttemptSurvivesTicks removes or omits the manager handle for a real live managed-attempt fixture, runs at least three ReconcileAt ticks, and proves the process remains alive.
2. TestSupervisorReconcile_LiveDiskOnlyAttemptSurvivesTicks proves the fresh claim remains in_progress and supervisor reconciliation does not create a replacement duplicate for that attempt.
3. TestSupervisorReconcile_LiveDiskOnlyAttemptSurvivesTicks proves preservation emits or observes a structured supervisor/lifecycle diagnostic containing worker ID, PID, bead ID, and preservation reason.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... -run "TestSupervisorReconcile_LiveDiskOnlyAttemptSurvivesTicks" passes.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
After restart, re-exec, or reconciliation, the server may have a live managed worker represented only by a disk record and no in-memory manager handle. Such a worker should survive supervisor ticks when its same-machine lease and heartbeat are fresh, and the supervisor must not start a replacement duplicate.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:270-279 sends every snapshot stale ID through stopStaleDiskEntry. Because stopStaleDiskEntry currently cleans a live PID before checking whether staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim refuses release, a disk-only live worker can be killed during reconciliation. The existing TestSupervisorReconcile_FreshClaimingWorkerSurvivesTicks at cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor_test.go:882-962 keeps the live worker in the manager handle map and uses stale fixture PID 0, so it cannot detect a live PID represented only by a stale disk entry.

PROPOSED FIX
Adjust supervisor reconciliation so live same-machine disk-only managed attempts with fresh bead leases or heartbeats are preserved or adopted instead of stopped, and ensure the desired-count reconciliation does not create a replacement duplicate for the same live attempt. Cover the case with a real live managed-attempt fixture whose manager handle is removed or omitted before multiple ReconcileAt ticks.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change desired worker count, generic process cleanup, provider parent-death behavior, or manual/server coordination owned by ddx-635ae251. Do not weaken cleanup of dead PIDs or genuinely stale leases. Do not broaden adoption semantics beyond live same-machine disk-only managed attempts with fresh claim evidence.

PARENT
Split from root regression bead "server: preserve live managed PIDs during stale-record cleanup".

DEPS
None.

acceptance:
1. TestManagedWorkerRecordsProcessGroup proves StartExecuteLoop creates a server-managed drain worker with nonzero PID and PGID in WorkerRecord and persisted status.json.
2. TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagRunsWorkLoop proves the hidden ddx work --server-managed <worker-id> entry point reads the persisted spec and runs the same execute-loop path used by current server-managed workers.
3. TestManagedWorkerProcessBoundarySkipsExternalReportedWorkers proves process-boundary recording is applied only to server-owned work workers, not external reported workers or interactive Claude/Codex sessions.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/server/... -run 'TestManagedWorkerRecordsProcessGroup|TestManagedWorkerServerManagedFlagRunsWorkLoop|TestManagedWorkerProcessBoundarySkipsExternalReportedWorkers' passes.
5. make install is run after the code change lands.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Server-managed drain workers are still started as in-process goroutines, so their WorkerRecord usually has PID zero and no PGID. The server cannot reliably target the ddx work process tree that later launches claude, codex, shell, or sleep descendants.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers.go:123-127 records only PID and has no persisted PGID. cli/internal/server/workers.go:192 defines WorkerManager as managing in-process work workers as goroutines. cli/internal/server/workers.go:438 creates a cancelable context, and cli/internal/server/workers.go:461-462 starts drainProgress and runWorker goroutines instead of a server-owned OS process. cli/internal/server/workers.go:414-436 writes the initial WorkerRecord before any managed worker process boundary exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a server-managed subprocess launch path for StartExecuteLoop in cli/internal/server/workers.go:361-464. Persist the ExecuteLoopWorkerSpec as today, then start the current ddx binary as ddx work --server-managed <worker-id> or an equivalent hidden internal entry point in its own process group. Record nonzero PID and PGID on WorkerRecord and status.json. Keep the existing in-process path only where tests explicitly inject it, and do not make externally reported workers look server-owned.

NON-SCOPE
Do not kill external reported workers or interactive Claude/Codex sessions. Do not change bead claim semantics except releasing claims for the stopped/reaped managed worker. Do not implement UI controls.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT AND RELATIONSHIP
Parent bead: ddx-9d1af129. Governing artifact reference: plan:server-managed-workers. No explicit dependency IDs were provided by the parent bead.

description:
PROBLEM: canonicalizing `design-tokens.json` to the `.stitch/DESIGN.md` warm palette and loading the Inter variable webfont both change rendered pixels on every page, so the committed baselines under `cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/screenshots.spec.ts-snapshots` (and `e2e/artifacts.spec.ts-snapshots`) no longer match. `e2e/screenshots.spec.ts:11-23` documents that these are the visual-regression baselines and that dark/light parity is a FEAT-008 frontend-design gate (`docs/helix/01-frame/concerns.md#frontend-design`) — every page is snapshotted in both modes and any theme-specific palette drift fails CI. Until the baselines are regenerated, `bun run test:e2e:visual` fails and the drift gate cannot distinguish an intended palette change from an unintended one.

ROOT CAUSE: pixel baselines are committed artifacts derived from the token + font inputs changed by the two sibling beads; they are not auto-derived at test time.

KNOWN HAZARD (from prior failed attempts on the parent bead — read before starting): (a) the harness resolved `/api/projects` against the machine-level repo root instead of the temp `ddx-e2e-*` fixture workspace, which trips the explicit guard at `e2e/screenshots.spec.ts:40-48` (`getFixtureIds` filters for a `ddx-e2e-` path/name and throws `fixture server has no ddx-e2e-* project registered` otherwise) — do NOT hand-bootstrap a DDx server; let `playwright.config.ts` start the fixture-backed server so the temp workspace is the registered project; (b) a direct `--update-snapshots` retry hit a Vite/Rolldown out-of-memory failure during the frontend build — if that recurs, raise the Node heap (e.g. `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`) rather than skipping the build.

PROPOSED FIX: with the sibling token and font beads landed, regenerate the visual baselines via `cd cli/internal/server/frontend && bunx playwright test e2e/screenshots.spec.ts --update-snapshots` (the procedure named in the header comment at `e2e/screenshots.spec.ts:12-14`), commit the regenerated PNGs, and confirm a clean re-run passes without `--update-snapshots`. Regenerate any other snapshot directory the suite reports as stale for the same reason. Inspect the diffs before committing: the new baselines must show the warm palette (cream `#F4EFE6` canvas, steel `#3B5B7A` accents) and Inter-rendered text — if a page still shows generic white/gray surfaces or purple/green accents, the sibling token bead is incomplete and this bead must report that rather than baking the drift in.

NON-SCOPE: editing `design-tokens.json`, `tailwind.config.js`, or `src/app.css` (both sibling beads own those files — this bead regenerates artifacts only); adding or removing pages from the screenshot matrix; changing per-page `tolerance` values to force a pass; introducing a display font; component-level `gray-*`/`blue-*` utility migration; any Go backend change.

description:
PROBLEM
BuildDDxBinary and BuildDDxFizeauTestSeamBinary create process-lifetime binary directories shared through sync.Once. After ddx-b2702b9f moves both directories beneath configured execution scratch, cleanup must eventually reclaim abandoned directories without deleting one still owned by a long-running test process. The cleanup allowlist currently recognizes ddx-fixture-bin-* but not ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*; adding the missing prefix without ownership evidence would make directory age alone sufficient to delete a live process-owned binary directory.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:87-95 stores both built binary paths in process-wide sync.Once state, and cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:119-167 creates and publishes the two binary directories without a durable owner marker.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:26-46 includes ddx-fixture-bin-* in defaultExecutionCleanupScratchPrefixes but omits ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:667-681 synthesizes ownership when cleanup.json is absent, while cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:728-755 removes an allowlisted directory after the age threshold when no liveness evidence preserves it.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:189-221 preserves a directory with live PID or lease evidence only when compatible metadata exists.
ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 establish the host-global trust and metadata-marked reclamation rules, but neither makes the fixture-binary producer emit process-lifetime ownership evidence.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a small lower-level scratch-owner marker contract that can be imported by both internal/testutils and internal/agent without an import cycle. The marker must record the resource kind, owner PID, creation time, and a process-start identity when the platform exposes one; marker writes must be atomic.
Have BuildDDxBinary and BuildDDxFizeauTestSeamBinary write the marker immediately after creating their directory and before caching or returning the binary path. If marker creation fails, remove the new directory and fail the build helper instead of publishing an unowned path.
Teach execution cleanup to recognize both ddx-fixture-bin-* and ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-* through the owner-marker contract. Preserve an old directory while its recorded owner process identity is live. Reclaim it only after the owner is dead or conclusively mismatched and the existing minimum-age requirement is satisfied.
When process identity cannot be validated safely, preserve the directory and emit a structured uncertain-owner observation. Missing or malformed markers must follow the ownership rules from ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93; a prefix alone is never host-global ownership proof.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go and fixture_repo_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go and execution_cleanup_test.go
- a small shared internal scratch-owner marker package and its tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not replace the process-wide sync.Once binary cache with t.TempDir.
Do not redesign general host-global scratch trust; ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 own that policy.
Do not reclaim a metadata-less or uncertain-owner host-global directory merely because its name matches a DDx prefix.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
ddx-b2702b9f must land first so both producers use the configured scratch root.
ddx-1eb1ba93 must land first so metadata-marked stale reclamation and host-global ownership rules are established; it already depends on ddx-05e3d16b.

description:
PROBLEM
The two embedded-dispatch runner tests isolate provider configuration by changing HOME to a raw ddx-home-* directory. On Niflheim, an abandoned ddx-home-3567057526 contained a 468 MB private Go module cache with read-only module directories. A later internal/agent gate discovered that prefix, recursively walked it, and produced more than 2.7 GB of Go test operation logs before continuing. Repeated gates can duplicate the module cache, leak inodes, and make cleanup expensive.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29-34 and cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:56-61 call os.MkdirTemp with an empty root, change HOME, and discard os.RemoveAll errors. Changing HOME also changes the default GOPATH and GOMODCACHE for any Go subprocess or embedded tool that does not receive explicit values. Downloaded module directories are commonly mode 0555, so the ignored cleanup error can leave the entire test HOME under the process-global temp root. These are the only ddx-home-* producers in cli/internal/agent.

PROPOSED FIX
Replace the raw os.MkdirTemp fixtures with a shared test helper backed by t.TempDir so cleanup failures are test failures. Before changing HOME, preserve an explicit stable Go module-cache/GOPATH policy for child work so the isolated provider-config HOME cannot become a second module cache. Add a tripwire that runs both embedded-dispatch paths and proves no HOME/go/pkg/mod tree and no new process-global ddx-home-* directory is created.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go
- nearest internal/agent test helper if shared setup is warranted

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production runner routing, make live provider calls, delete existing host scratch, or change production cleanup ownership/budgets. ddx-f914dddd and ddx-de1ff4b4 own those cleanup changes.

PARENT
ddx-6a2ce3bd.

DEPS
None; this test-producer repair can land independently of the production scratch-root helper children.

description:
PROBLEM
Forwarded federation writes need an autonomous idempotency proof. Retrying the same hub-issued command with the same request id must replay the original result and must not launch duplicate workers, append duplicate bead events, or write the same document twice.

ROOT CAUSE
- docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-002-server-web-ui.md:338 defines TC-017.5 idempotency for federated worker commands.
- docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-002-server-web-ui.md:379 defines TC-020.6 idempotency for mutating managed-node commands.
- docs/helix/06-iterate/server-operator-workbench-plan-2026-06-08.md:98-102 requires forwarded commands to carry request id, target node/project, and expected version metadata.
- Existing GraphQL idempotency tests such as cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_mutation_runs_test.go:101-154 and resolver_operator_prompt_test.go:218-231 cover local idempotency surfaces, but the federation owner-write path needs its own forwarded-command coverage.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add focused Go tests or live multi-process tests for forwarded federation write idempotency.
- Use the same request id/idempotency key for two identical hub-issued worker, bead, or document write commands.
- Assert the second response returns the original result/deduplicated state and does not duplicate spoke-local state.
- Cover at least two command classes: worker start and one persistent data mutation (`beadCreate` or `documentWrite`).
- Keep the test deterministic with loopback servers and synthetic request ids; do not rely on wall-clock sleeps beyond short polling for process readiness.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not build a new global idempotency framework unless existing request-id plumbing cannot support the tests.
- Do not add real network/tailnet tests.
- Do not change unrelated local run/operator-prompt idempotency behavior.

PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-c6317784 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 5 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
# PROBLEM
The bead backend interface today (`cli/internal/bead/backend.go`) is JSONL-shaped: `RawBackend` requires whole-corpus `ReadAll`/`WriteAll`, and `Backend` declares only 22 of `*Store`'s 69 public methods. Per TD-027 (the canonical Bead Storage System and Lifecycle spec), the bead architecture needs:

- A typed `Operation` pattern with `Apply(b *Bead) error` (CAS via error returns)
- 11 LSP-clean storage sub-interfaces composing `Backend`
- Pluggable `IDGenerator` and parallel `LifecycleSubscriber`
- `context.Context` first-parameter discipline on every interface method
- Sentinel errors (`ErrNotFound`, `ErrConflict`, `ErrInvalidID`, `ErrAlreadyClaimed`, `ErrNotClaimedByOwner`, `ErrUnsupported`)
- The optional `OperationApplier` interface on `RawBackend` so JSONL backends can preserve heartbeat sidecar optimization
- A canonical Bead data model (field enumeration + invariants + JSONL wire format + schema-versioning policy)

This bead lays the foundation that all per-concern beads (L/C/E/X/Q/D/A/MIG) depend on. It declares the event reader/writer interfaces but deliberately does not migrate `AppendEvent`, `Events`, or `EventsByKind`; the E bead owns event-method ctx threading and `*Store` event interface satisfaction.

# ROOT CAUSE
- `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:10-67` — `RawBackend` (4 whole-corpus methods) + `Backend` (22 high-level methods, incomplete).
- `cli/internal/bead/store.go` — `*Store` exposes 69 public methods, none take `ctx context.Context`.
- `cli/internal/bead/axon_backend.go:340-381` — `WriteAll` ships entire corpus per mutation (catastrophic for Postgres).
- Operation pattern, IDGenerator, sentinel errors, context discipline — all absent.
- Bead data model (the canonical schema of fields + invariants) — only implicit in the Go struct.

# PROPOSED FIX
Implement TD-027 §5–§13 foundation pieces that are required before the per-concern beads can execute.

## New files

1. `cli/internal/bead/operation.go` — `Operation` interface with `Apply(b *Bead) error`. `MutateFunc` adapter for ad-hoc mutations. Empty named-op section (per-concern beads add their op types).
2. `cli/internal/bead/id.go` — `ValidateID`, format constants (`DefaultIDPrefix`, `MaxIDLength`, `MinIDLength`), `IDGenerator` interface, `RandomHexIDGenerator`, `SequentialIDGenerator`, `NewIDGenerator()` default.
3. `cli/internal/bead/errors.go` — sentinel e
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Sentinel errors declared as distinct `error` values. Test: `TestSentinelErrors_AreErrorValues`.
- Context typed accessors implemented. Tests: `TestWithIdentity_RoundTrip`, `TestIdentityFromContext_AbsentReturnsFalse`, `TestWithTrace_RoundTrip`.
- Foundational sub-interfaces (`BeadInitializer`, `BeadReader`, `BeadLifecycle`, `BeadEventReader`, `BeadEventWriter`) declared with ctx-first signatures. `*Store` satisfies only the non-event foundation interfaces in this bead — compile-time assertions: `var _ BeadInitializer = (*Store)(nil)`, `var _ BeadReader = (*Store)(nil)`, `var _ BeadLifecycle = (*Store)(nil)`. description:
PROBLEM
Execute-bead providers can launch a focused test and the full package suite concurrently. On 2026-07-13, the ddx-12a41acc provider stated that it would run the exact focused regex first and only then the full internal/agent suite, but emitted both tool calls in the same turn. That duplicated Go compilation, started the expensive suite before the focused proof was known green, and increased the chance of CPU and provider-process fan-out.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2112 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2139-2147 require git/index mutations to be sequential but do not impose the same ordering on validation commands. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2085-2094 governs reruns of long commands but does not forbid overlapping focused tests, full suites, linters, or lefthook. Rich harnesses may issue multiple shell tool calls concurrently in one model turn, so narrative intent to run focused-then-full is not an execution constraint.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared execute-bead instruction requiring validation gates to run sequentially: wait for focused tests to complete successfully before launching broader package/workspace tests, then wait before lint or pre-commit. Explicitly forbid overlapping go test, cargo test, npm test, make test, and lefthook invocations in the same attempt. Preserve legitimate parallelism inside a single build/test command.

NON-SCOPE
Do not globally disable model tool parallelism, serialize read-only inspection, reduce language toolchain internal parallelism, skip any required gate, or weaken test timeouts. Resource enforcement and host-wide concurrency caps remain owned by ddx-c4cbf253 and ddx-93f6041e.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-5958e8a. Depends on ddx-aa6cc320 so its internal/agent verification cannot launch real provider fixtures.

description:
PROBLEM
An execute-bead agent that correctly writes status: open in no_changes_rationale.txt while leaving an uncommitted implementation patch is still sent through a synthesized iteration commit and the full staged pre-commit gate. Live attempt 20260713T105612-7589dd4a spent more than a minute in the race hook after a 745.706-second diagnostic failure, even though the agent explicitly requested retry and no land. This turns the fallback contract into another expensive mixed-result attempt and can discard useful dirty work after classification.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1314-1377 checks IsDirty and calls SynthesizeCommit before reading the bundle rationale. Only afterward, cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1415-1448 reads no_changes_rationale.txt and classifies a synthesized implementation commit plus rationale as mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale. Because RealGitOps.SynthesizeCommit invokes git commit, cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:148-218 also runs repository hooks before DDx learns that the attempt was explicitly retryable.

PROPOSED FIX
Read and parse the bundle no_changes_rationale.txt before the synthesis branch. When a valid status: open, status: proposed, status: blocked, or verification_command rationale is present and the agent made no explicit commit, do not call SynthesizeCommit. Preserve any dirty implementation diff as a durable rescue patch in the execution bundle, attach its path to the result, then classify the rationale normally. Retain synthesized commits for dirty successful exits without a rationale, and retain fail-closed mixed-result rejection when the agent itself made an implementation commit and also wrote a rationale.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken mixed_commit_and_no_changes_rationale rejection, skip required gates for successful implementation commits, change no-changes retry/close policy, or automatically land the preserved dirty patch.

PARENT
None; root execute-bead fallback-contract regression observed during the Niflheim queue drain.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify to route to the Axon importer in verification mode and report verification success through both command output and JSON stats. This should be testable without coupling to importer storage internals.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The CLI reads flags at cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go:44 and routes --to-axon into Migrator.MigrateToAxon at cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go:55. The relevant flag registration is at cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go:202, and the importer stats shape is defined at cli/internal/bead/migrate.go:609. Without a verify-mode routing test, --to-axon --verify can be accepted by the CLI but fail to pass Verify true or fail to expose verification status to operators.

PROPOSED FIX
Update cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go and cmd tests so --to-axon --verify routes Verify true into Migrator.MigrateToAxon and prints or returns verification success when the migrator succeeds. Ensure JSON and human output expose bead, event, attachment, dry-run, verify, and limit values from the migrator stats.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- Storage importer internals except as needed to satisfy the Migrator interface; sibling children own importer apply/fidelity behavior.
- New backend selection policy outside the existing Migrator/NewStore construction path.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.
- Help text, invalid flag-combination rejection, dry-run routing, and apply routing are owned by sibling child beads.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
TD-027.

DEPENDENCY TO PRESERVE WHEN FILING
Parent dependency ID ddx-3d96c6f9.

description:
PROBLEM
procExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessScanner.inspect (cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:57-74) drops a process entirely -- it is never even offered to classification -- whenever os.Readlink("/proc/<pid>/cwd") fails or returns empty (execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:63,70-72), or when the resolved cwd no longer maps to any known root. Such a process is invisible to the leftover-worktree scan even though it may still hold open files inside a leased worktree (design: docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-040-leftover-worktree-process-reaping.md, "Change 2").

ROOT CAUSE
Worktree attribution today has exactly one signal: cwd (executionCleanupAttemptProcessFromWorkerStatus, execution_cleanup_process.go:415-437, fed from procExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessScanner.inspect at execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:63). If proc.Worktree ends up empty, inspect returns `(executionCleanupAttemptProcess{}, false)` at execution_cleanup_process_linux.go:70-72 and the process is dropped from the scan entirely -- it never reaches classifyExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessGroup, so it can never be reaped no matter how long it has been orphaned.

PROPOSED FIX
In procExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessScanner.inspect, when cwd-based attribution yields an empty Worktree, add a fallback: enumerate /proc/<pid>/fd/*, resolve each entry's symlink target (best-effort, skipping unreadable descriptors), and apply the same root-truncation rule used for cwd attribution (reuse or extract the truncate-to-root helper introduced or existing in execution_cleanup_process.go) against each resolved target. The first fd target that truncates to a root under the configured tempRoot becomes Worktree. This is strictly additive: cwd-based attribution keeps priority, and a process with no cwd signal and no matching fd signal remains unclassified (excluded from the scan, never killed), preserving today's conservative default.

NON-SCOPE
- No change to the classification/kill-safety logic in classifyExecutionCleanupAttemptProcessGroup -- this bead only widens the detection signal feeding it.
- No non-Linux implementation -- mirrors the existing execution_cleanup_process_other.go no-op split.
- No change to the cwd-based root-normalization fix (separate child bead, ddx-79dab565).

description:
PROBLEM
On 2026-07-07 the multi-project workers stopped making steady claim progress because /tmp had zero free inodes. Cayce emitted repeated picker.claim_race events with `bead: create claim liveness tmp: open /tmp/ddx-claim-heartbeats/...: no space left on device`, while resource.preflight continued to report status=ok because it checked /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt and project evidence roots, not the claim-liveness root. Manual cleanup restored /tmp from 0 free inodes to ~347k free inodes and Cayce immediately claimed cayce-a9775904.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/bead/claim_liveness.go:31-35 hardcodes claim heartbeat sidecars under `filepath.Join(os.TempDir(), "ddx-claim-heartbeats", ...)`.
cli/internal/bead/claim_liveness.go:56-64 creates atomic temp files in that directory and returns `bead: create claim liveness tmp` when /tmp has no inodes.
cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:250-267 enforces byte/inode thresholds only for roots passed into execution resource preflight, and current worker preflight evidence showed those roots excluded /tmp/ddx-claim-heartbeats.

PROPOSED FIX
Add the claim-liveness temp root to pre-claim resource preflight so inode exhaustion is detected before claim attempts loop as claim races. Prefer moving claim liveness under the configured DDx execution temp root or a project-scoped runtime root instead of raw os.TempDir(), but preserve stale-claim detection across workers on the same machine. Add cleanup for stale tmp files under ddx-claim-heartbeats and include reclaimed inode counts in resource.preflight events.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change bead claim semantics or heartbeat TTL. Do not remove durable worker/evidence history. Do not weaken cross-worker stale-claim protection.
