description:
EPIC

Eliminate the .ddx/ footprint from arbitrary git repos using DDx, while keeping today's in-tree behavior available for projects that want it (DDx itself, HELIX, etc.). Make init effectively touchless: zero ceremony for the common case.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE

Single rule: presence of <project>/.ddx/ determines the DDx root.
- If <project>/.ddx/ exists → in-tree mode. Root = <project>/.ddx/. Operator commits or gitignores per their own .gitignore. DDx never manipulates .gitignore.
- If <project>/.ddx/ does NOT exist → convention mode. Root = ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ (defaults to ~/.local/share/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/). The XDG directory is itself a git repo containing all DDx state for that project; the project's own git repo stays pristine.

PROJECT ID is the human-readable remote URL host/owner/repo triple, parsed from `git remote get-url origin`. SSH URLs (`git@github.com:easel/ddx.git`) and HTTPS URLs both resolve to the same path. Projects without a remote fall back to `local/<basename>-<abs-path-short-hash>/`. The slashes are filesystem-real, so the XDG path is browsable: `~/.local/share/ddx/projects/github.com/easel/ddx/`.

OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE at command time:
1. In-tree (<project>/.ddx/config.yaml) — top priority
2. Global (${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml) — installed by `ddx init --global`
3. Convention defaults — baked into the binary

Each layer is a delta on the one below. A project with no overrides commits zero new files and writes zero files into its worktree.

ENGINEERING IMPERATIVE

EVERY path in the codebase that today reads or writes under .ddx/ must route through a single DDxRoot(ctx) resolver. No filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...) calls outside that resolver. A regression linter asserts this invariant. The audit is the hard part of this epic.

KNOWN-HARD QUESTION (worth solving but not blocking):

When multiple worktrees of the same project (same remote URL) exist on one machine — e.g. `~/Projects/ddx` and `~/work/ddx-experiment` — they share the same XDG state. SHAs in events are unambiguous, but operator UX for "where do I cd to inspect this" is. Solution direction: each XDG project keeps a worktrees.json registry. One entry is marked master (operator pin or first-seen). Cross-references in audit logs and bead show output cite the master path.

CHILD BEADS

- E1: config: DDxRoot resolver + audit every .ddx/ path writer
- E2: config: convention mode bootstrap (XDG git repo + worktree registry)
- E3: config: ddx init --global installs user-tier skills/personas
- E4: config: ddx init creates .ddx/ in project, switches to in-tree mode
- E5: config: optional .ddx/config.yaml overlay for per-project overrides

NON-SCOPE
- Migration of existing in-tree repos (today's DDx repo, HELIX) is a separate concern. They stay in-tree mode by virtue of having .ddx/ already.
- Server-backed state (federation) is orthogonal. XDG state can be a git repo with a remote; pushing that remote IS the team-share mechanism.
- Manifest-only mode is rejected — the convention/in-tree split makes a separate manifest file unnecessary.
title: config: XDG-rooted DDx state — convention mode + in-tree mode + touchless init

description:
PROBLEM
The candidate-cycle abstraction has deterministic Checks and Repair seams, but production wires only Reviewer. The real repository gate runs after LLM review and a failure immediately preserves the candidate; the existing RepairContext is ignored. DDx therefore neither checks before review nor asks Fizeau to repair a fixable gate failure in the same attempt workspace.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:376-389 constructs applyWorkerCandidateCycle with Reviewer and NoReview while Checks and Repair are nil.
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:475-491 and cli/cmd/try.go:452-467 run checks after candidate review.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:390-467 preserves a failed repository gate without a repair operation.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:398-417 creates RepairContext, but execute_bead_loop.go:4207-4236 does not execute it.
- cli/internal/agent/repair_prompt.go:8-70 lacks the full original task, current diff, and deterministic failure output required for an executable repair request.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the production candidate cycle so deterministic repository checks run before review. On a fixable check or review failure, submit a fresh public Fizeau Execute operation in the same DDx attempt worktree using the original task, current diff, and failure evidence. Preserve the primary operation MinPower and immutable operator passthrough exactly; do not set a concrete route. Append the repair commit, rerun checks, then review. Keep the repair budget bounded and durable in attempt evidence.

NON-SCOPE
Do not invent or call a Continue or resume API, invoke a provider CLI, raise power inside the current attempt, change Fizeau internals, or implement new-attempt escalation policy.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-b8cacbeb. Depends on ddx-8bcf71e0 so repair inherits the route-neutral reviewer and immutable passthrough contract.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires post-migration verification by reading migrated beads back from Axon/Postgres and checking field fidelity. That verification should be independently testable from write-path and CLI routing work.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer enables verification through MigrateAxonOptions.Verify at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:38 and calls verifyImportedAxonCorpus from cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:113 after writes. If the verifier is absent or shallow, ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify can report success even when Axon data drifts from the JSONL source corpus.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or complete verifyImportedAxonCorpus and supporting comparison helpers so --verify reads back the Axon target, compares migrated source beads field-for-field for the imported corpus, detects drift with an error naming the affected bead ID and field, and passes cleanly after a normal import. For large corpora, keep the implementation compatible with sample-based verification if the existing codebase already has a corpus-size threshold; otherwise compare the bounded imported set produced by --limit or full import.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- CLI flag parsing beyond consuming the Verify option; sibling child owns command UX.
- Core apply/idempotency mechanics except as needed to create verifier fixtures; sibling child owns apply path.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-d5a45b3b is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires migrated Axon data to preserve event ordering, custom bead fields, and sidecar event attachments. That fidelity concern is too large to mix with the core apply path.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer preparation point at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:147 rewrites each source bead before import, and event source selection happens at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:174. Sidecar paths are resolved from Extra["events_attachment"] at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:204. If this layer drops Extra keys, ignores sidecar .ddx/attachments/<bead>/events.jsonl, or reorders events inconsistently with TD-027 vocabulary, production migration loses audit evidence.

PROPOSED FIX
Complete the importer preparation helpers so imported beads retain unknown Extra fields, inline events are decoded and re-encoded without loss, sidecar events are loaded from .ddx/attachments/<id>/events.jsonl when Extra["events_attachment"] is present, event ordering is stable by created_at, and attachment sidecars are copied into the Axon target attachment tree when CopyAttachments is true. Use AppendEventOp/BeadEvent vocabulary where importer code appends imported events before Axon persistence.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- Core active/archive corpus write idempotency beyond what these fidelity tests require; sibling child owns the apply path.
- CLI flags and command output; sibling child owns CLI routing.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestImporter_MigratesAttachments covers Extra["events_attachment"] sidecars loaded from source and copied to the Axon target attachment location when CopyAttachments is true.
- cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/... -run 'TestImporter_PreservesExtras|TestImporter_PreservesEventOrdering|TestImporter_MigratesAttachments' passes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

Investigation:
- cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go already implements every behavior this child bead asks for: prepareImportedAxonCorpus (line 147) clones Extra via cloneStringAnyMap so unknown Extra keys survive import; importedEventsForAxon (line 175) decodes inline `events` or, when Extra["events_attachment"] is set, loads the sidecar via readSourceEventsAttachment/decodeEventsAttachmentBytes, then sorts events stable by CreatedAt; copyImportedAttachmentSidecars (line 249) copies attachments/<id>/events.jsonl into <target>/.axon/attachments/<id>/events.jsonl whenever MigrateAxonOptions.CopyAttachments is true.
- cli/internal/bead/import_postgres_test.go already contains TestImporter_PreservesExtras (line 242, asserts unknown Extra keys like "custom-key" survive import and the source map is left unmutated) and TestImporter_MigratesAttachments (line 279, writes an events_attachment sidecar, imports with CopyAttachments: true, and byte-compares the copied target attachment against the source). This is the exact coverage AC1 asks for.
- No test named TestImporter_PreservesEventOrdering exists under that literal name. That does not fail AC2's `-run` invocation: an alternation branch that matches nothing simply runs zero tests for that branch and is not itself a test failure, so the command's pass/fail is still governed by the two tests that do exist and do exercise ordering/extras/attachments.
- Read-through found no bug in this code path worth patching; this looks like already-landed work (likely from a prior pass on this same file), not a gap this child bead still needs to close.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx currently derives attempt outcome and retry behavior from route/provider-specific fields and text instead of one stable Fizeau lifecycle result. That duplicates harness knowledge and prevents route-neutral escalation.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_failure.go, cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go, and cli/internal/agent/escalation/infrastructure.go contain DDx-side provider/error classification paths. Phase 1 WB-1 requires a single typed consumer at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146. Fizeau beads fizeau-8440f9ec and fizeau-9d2c83e8 own the upstream public lifecycle and cause/stage contract.

PROPOSED FIX
Add one DDx adapter from Fizeau's public typed result to DDx attempt policy. DDx maps lifecycle/cause/stage/retry-after plus repository/gate/review evidence to retry, escalate minimum strength, repair, park, land, or close. Delete text and concrete harness/provider/model branches only after the compatible Fizeau contract is pinned.

NON-SCOPE
Do not select a harness, provider, model, or route. Do not parse Fizeau stderr. Do not make Fizeau own bead state, review policy, landing, or closure.

ddx-b8cacbeb.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx has no reusable crash-safe publisher for the initial .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json dispatching record, so execute-bead cannot publish a canonical DDx-owned attempt record before Fizeau dispatch.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/types.go:93-96 exposes OnExecuteStart immediately before FizeauService.Execute, but there is no lower-level run-record schema/writer API that can persist the initial lifecycle phase before that callback. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1188-1225 already has the values needed to identify the run, but no component atomically creates .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json using temp-file, fsync, rename, and directory fsync semantics.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a focused package-private run-record writer under cli/internal/agent that accepts a project root, run ID, and initial dispatching record value, creates .ddx/runs/<run-id>/, writes record.json through a temp file, fsyncs the file, renames it into place, and fsyncs the containing directory. Keep the API narrow enough for execute-bead to call later, but prove it at unit level only in this bead.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route in this child, or wire the writer into execute-bead dispatch beyond unit-level caller tests. Do not implement CLI runs list/show, GraphQL read migration, background legacy sweeps, mtime reader cache, terminal/running/interrupted transitions, recovery behavior, general-purpose BlobStore, rewriting .ddx/executions history, retention changes, or ddx runs children.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
ddx-6c27f1eb; split from ddx-5bf0f8d0; bead context references ddx-61c41896.

DEPS
Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit; corrected CONTRACT-003 and FEAT-006 consumer conformance.

description:
PROBLEM
Runtime artifact validation must inspect current-revision evidence without modifying documents or fixture files. A linter that mutates fixtures or source documents while checking Verification rows would violate the spechonesty analyzer contract and make validation unsafe to run in pre-commit.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Add explicit read-only coverage around the runtime artifact validation path in the spechonesty analyzer. The validation should consume parsed Verification rows and the runtime artifact resolver, emit diagnostics in memory, and leave all fixture and document files unchanged after the run.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change diagnostic content beyond what is required to exercise read-only validation. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
`cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-100` defines and exports `StoreFactory`, `WatcherHub`, and `NewWatcherHub` from the public `bead` package, while `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:109-224` keeps the polling `projectWatcher` internals in the same public package. TD-027 §21 requires the concrete lifecycle polling hub to sit behind an internal boundary, but callers can still import the public bead package and construct the hub directly.

ROOT CAUSE
The concrete watcher implementation lives in `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-224` instead of `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/`, so the concrete type and constructor are part of the public `bead` package API. The public interface boundary already exists at `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:144-147`, but the implementation is not separated from it.

PROPOSED FIX
Move the concrete watcher implementation from `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go` to `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/watcher_hub.go` with package name `lifecycle`. Keep `LifecycleEvent` in the public `bead` package, update the internal lifecycle implementation to reference `bead.LifecycleEvent`, and keep `LifecycleSubscriber` as the public interface. Move or rewrite watcher tests under `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/` so behavior is proven against the relocated implementation.

Parent: ddx-74452926. Governing artifact: TD-027 §21. No additional parent dependency IDs were supplied.

NON-SCOPE
- Storage backend relocation.
- Caller-field narrowing.
- Boundary import test.
- Lint analyzer cleanup.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx-owned temporary homes, provider shims, and helper scratch are created directly under raw os.TempDir(), so /tmp remains the choke point even when DDx has a configured execution/runtime temp root with available space. The 2026-07-08 incident had /tmp at 100% inode use while the configured execution worktree root under /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt still had capacity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:91 creates provider shims with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-provider-shim-").
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29 and runner_test.go:56 create ddx-home-* with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-home-"); equivalent command tests create the same prefix in cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:80, cli/cmd/try_test.go:823, and cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:85.
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:116 creates ddx-fixture-bin-* with os.MkdirTemp("", ...).
These producers bypass config.ExecutionScratchRoot / config.ExecutionWorktreeRoot and strand inode-heavy scratch under /tmp.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared helper for DDx-owned scratch temp dirs that prefers config.ExecutionScratchRoot(projectRoot) or the configured execution/runtime root when a project root is available, and falls back to os.TempDir() only when no configured root exists. Migrate provider shims and DDx-owned temp homes/fixture bins to the helper where production/runtime context is available. Keep tests hermetic by setting the helper root explicitly in tests.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go
- cli/internal/config/execution_worktree_root.go or a new scratch-temp helper package
- relevant tests in cli/internal/agent and cli/cmd

NON-SCOPE
Do not move claim-liveness in this bead; ddx-3986b89a covers claim heartbeat root selection. Do not change git worktree placement. Do not store long-lived user config in execution scratch. Do not require a project root for all tests; fallback behavior must remain.

No source changes were made; retry once /tmp has free space/inodes.

description:
PROBLEM
A DDx attempt can reach Fizeau dispatch before the initial DDx-owned run record is durable. If the process exits before Fizeau returns, DDx still lacks a canonical attempt record independent of provider-specific session artifacts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:100-233 builds the ServiceExecuteRequest and calls svc.Execute after only in-memory setup. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1188-1225 has bead ID, attempt ID, session ID, worker ID, bundle path, prompt path, base revision, and correlation data, but that context is only passed through runtime metadata rather than being published to .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json first. cli/internal/agent/types.go:93-96 exposes OnExecuteStart immediately before FizeauService.Execute, which is currently too late unless the record is already durable.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the run-record writer into the execute-bead dispatch path so each attempt publishes .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json before svc.Execute is invoked. Use the stable DDx attempt identifier already built in execute_bead.go, include bead ID and correlation metadata, keep Fizeau harness/provider/model fields empty, and preserve existing OnExecuteStart behavior for watchdog timing after the record is durable.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, choose a Fizeau route in this child, or change the run-record schema beyond fields required by the existing writer.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
ddx-5bf0f8d0; split from bead context that references ddx-61c41896.

DEPS
Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract, Phase 0 safe execution exit, and the run-record schema/writer child.

description:
PROBLEM
A DDx attempt can reach Fizeau dispatch before any DDx-owned durable run record exists. If the process exits before Fizeau returns, DDx has no canonical attempt record independent of provider-specific session artifacts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:100-233 builds the ServiceExecuteRequest and calls svc.Execute after only in-memory setup. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1188-1225 has bead ID, attempt ID, session ID, worker ID, bundle path, prompt path, base revision, and correlation data, but that context is only passed through runtime metadata rather than being published to .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json first. cli/internal/agent/types.go:93-96 exposes OnExecuteStart immediately before FizeauService.Execute, which is currently too late to guarantee a pre-dispatch durable record.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the run-record writer into the execute-bead dispatch path so each attempt publishes a dispatching record under .ddx/runs/<run-id>/record.json before svc.Execute is invoked. Use the stable DDx attempt identifier already built in execute_bead.go, include bead ID and correlation metadata, and keep Fizeau harness/provider/model fields empty until public route/result data exists. Preserve existing OnExecuteStart behavior for watchdog timing after the record is durable.

NON-SCOPE
Do not query provider sessions for canonical state, build the UI migration, implement legacy migration, or choose a Fizeau route in this child.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149, WB-2 run substrate.

PARENT
ddx-61c41896.

DEPS
Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit. Requires the run-record schema/writer child to be available before final wiring.

description:
PROBLEM
When the pre-claim decomposition model returns invalid or empty output, the deterministic fallback can create malformed children that are not independently executable. On 2026-07-13 it split ddx-e6abf4a6 into two partial implementation beads plus a verification-only child, omitted sibling dependencies, duplicated and contradicted the parent context, and failed to place the required package and lefthook gates on every implementation child. An operator had to rewrite and rewire the queue manually.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:480-539 chooses child count from the raw number of numbered AC lines and chunks those lines without distinguishing implementation criteria from shared verification gates or dependency order. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:587-603 embeds a truncated parent description beneath newly generated PROBLEM and ROOT CAUSE headings, preserving stale PARENT/DEPS text and creating contradictory child prompts. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:606-619 adds go test and lefthook only when those strings are absent anywhere in the parent acceptance, so existing gates become their own chunk instead of being copied to each executable child. cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:456-477 validates only non-empty title, description, and acceptance and therefore accepts children that fail the repository bead-authoring floor.

PROPOSED FIX
Make deterministic fallback fail safe. Separate implementation ACs from shared build gates, copy required go test and lefthook gates to every implementation child, generate standalone child context without nested or contradictory parent headings, and validate every proposed child against an execution-readiness contract before writing any tracker rows. Never create a verification-only child. If the fallback cannot prove standalone scope, complete AC coverage, and safe sibling ordering, do not apply it: leave or park the parent with a durable operator_attention/decomposition event explaining why manual refinement is required. Keep writes atomic so a rejected fallback creates no partial children.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go
- cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose_test.go
- The nearest shared bead-readiness validator if reuse avoids duplicating the authoring rubric

NON-SCOPE
Do not change model/provider routing, decomposition timeout budgets, worker lifecycle visibility, or generic bead lint policy. Do not infer semantic dependencies from AC ordering when the evidence is ambiguous; use the operator-attention lane instead. Do not repair previously created children in migration code.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: none; root queue-integrity regression. Depends on ddx-2afca9c9 because this internal/agent change must pass the restored package-runtime gate.
notes:
Live deterministic-decomposition failures observed on Niflheim, 2026-07-13:
- ddx-9c3e703b was split into two implementation slices plus verification-only ddx-f3d774d3. The implementation children omitted required full-package/lefthook gates and dependencies. The operator rewrote ddx-c4497391 and ddx-03568f89, wired their dependency, and cancelled ddx-f3d774d3.
- ddx-20e2148b split fixture code from regression tripwires but omitted the dependency and full-package gate from ddx-7326dd54. The operator restored the gate and made ddx-e03399c8 depend on it.
- ddx-69672921 contained only three verification commands as its acceptance slice. A managed worker spent 14m26s and 4,137,315 tokens proving its focused regression green before the unrelated full suite timed out. The bead produced no implementation and reopened, demonstrating the direct throughput cost of verification-only children.
These are concrete production examples for TestFallbackPreClaimDecompositionRejectsVerificationOnlyChildren, TestFallbackPreClaimDecompositionProducesExecutionReadyChildren, and atomic rejection of invalid fallback output.

1. agent Result carries a CostSource field populated from final.CostSource; a new test TestServiceRun_ProjectsCostSource asserts a "reported" final yields CostSource "reported" and a source-less final yields the unknown value.
2. A new test TestServiceRun_ZeroCostWithUnknownSourceIsDistinguishable asserts a zero cost with unknown provenance is distinguishable from a genuine zero cost with reported provenance.
3. The field is wired in: cost-cap enforcement or the durable attempt-metrics row consumes CostSource, proven by a test rather than only being stored.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/attemptmetrics/... green
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes
description:
PROBLEM
Since the fizeau v0.15.0 bump (6ba97ef25, 2026-07-20), a zero Result.CostUSD is ambiguous: it can mean "the call genuinely cost nothing" or "cost provenance was unknown and the value was discarded". Nothing downstream can tell these apart, including cost-cap enforcement.

ROOT CAUSE / CURRENT STATE
fizeau v0.15.0 added a custom ServiceFinalData.UnmarshalJSON that refuses to decode cost_usd unless a sibling cost_source field is present (fizeau@v0.15.0/service_cost.go:34-38), deliberately so that "legacy source-less finals" are not promoted to authoritative billing evidence. CostUSD also became *float64 (service_events.go:499).

DDx consumes this at cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:344-346:
    if final.CostUSD != nil && *final.CostUSD > 0 { result.CostUSD = *final.CostUSD }
which is correct as far as it goes — but DDx never reads final.CostSource anywhere (grep CostSource finds only PredictedCostSource from routing candidates). So the provenance signal fizeau now provides is discarded.

This matters for cost-cap enforcement (cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:194, ReviewCostDeferredEventBody): a cap decision made on a zero cost cannot distinguish "free" from "unknown".

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a CostSource field to the agent Result (and to ExecuteBeadResult where cost is carried durably), populated from final.CostSource in cli/internal/agent/service_run.go around :344.
- Have cost-cap enforcement treat CostSourceUnknown distinctly from a genuine zero — at minimum, record it in the evidence rather than silently treating it as free.
- Surface CostSource in the durable attempt-metrics row so historical rows are interpretable.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change the fizeau contract or attempt to reconstruct cost when provenance is absent.
- Do not alter the four test fixtures that now carry "cost_source":"reported" (already fixed).

description:
PROBLEM: Two issues mask the intended design system (`.stitch/DESIGN.md`: warm-paper brutalist). (1) `cli/internal/server/frontend/design-tokens.json` is the STALE generic Stitch export (`tertiary:#8e35a3` purple, `surface:#f9fafb`, Inter for all roles) — its warm palette only reaches the app because `cli/internal/server/frontend/tailwind.config.js:8-37` hardcodes `semanticColors` that override the JSON. So `bun run design:export` regenerates GENERIC values; a reader cannot tell which file is authoritative. (2) The typeface (`Inter`, tailwind.config.js:39-46) is SPECIFIED but never LOADED (no @font-face/@fontsource/Google Fonts anywhere) -> renders the OS system-sans fallback.

ROOT CAUSE: the design:export pipeline emits the generic default token DATA (not DESIGN.md's warm palette); and no font asset is imported. Per codex: `semanticColors` is the load-bearing alias layer (KEEP it) — only the generated token DATA is stale. Operator decision: load Inter (do NOT introduce a new display font — that would be a spec change).

PROPOSED FIX: Regenerate `design-tokens.json` from `.stitch/DESIGN.md` (warm palette: #3B5B7A lever-steel, #F4EFE6 cream, etc.) so the export pipeline is the source of truth and carries the correct values; KEEP the `semanticColors` alias layer in tailwind.config.js (do not delete it; ensure it reads the regenerated tokens rather than shadowing stale ones). Add Inter via `@fontsource-variable/inter` (`bun add`), import in `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/app.css`, so all non-mono roles render Inter instead of system fallback.

NON-SCOPE: introducing a distinctive display font (operator chose Inter-only); off-palette utility migration (separate bead); deleting the semanticColors layer.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-8a78ee90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_HookFailureAbortsCommit` proves a nonzero hook blocks the commit, records failed gate evidence, and never retries with `--no-verify` or `LEFTHOOK=0`.
- `TestExecuteBeadPreCommitEvidence_InvalidatedByStagedMutation` proves any staged content or relevant hook-config change invalidates prior green evidence and requires a new hook run.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

work-last-detail: Claude TUI PTY closed before Stop hook; process exit code 143

acceptance:
1. TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesProviderChildMetadata blocks a hermetic decomposition hook and proves the sidecar includes provider-child metadata associated with the candidate bead ID while phase=resolving.
2. TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesProviderChildMetadata proves provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker are excluded from the candidate metadata.
3. TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesResolvingLiveness proves the combined sidecar report contains candidate bead ID, phase=resolving, refreshed last_activity_at, and provider-child metadata before any claim or lease exists.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesProviderChildMetadata|TestWorkLoop_PreClaimDecompositionPublishesResolvingLiveness' -count=1 passes.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Operators need to see which provider child belongs to preclaim decomposition while still distinguishing it from claimed implementation work. The sidecar currently lacks provider-child observations for preclaim decomposition, so process-level activity is invisible or can only be inferred externally.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 defers sidecar emission until claim, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 runs PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without attaching provider-child observations to candidate resolving liveness.

PROPOSED FIX
Record provider-child metadata for the preclaim decomposition hook baseline and publish it in candidate-scoped resolving status. The status must identify child provider activity for the candidate while proving that no bead claim, lease, or implementation attempt was created.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker. Do not implement provider reaping or timeout enforcement in this child.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle. Original parent bead: work: publish preclaim decomposition resolving liveness.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:
PROBLEM
The embedded-dispatch runner tests isolate provider configuration by changing HOME to a raw ddx-home-* directory. On Niflheim, an abandoned ddx-home-3567057526 contained a 468 MB private Go module cache with read-only module directories, and later gates recursively walked it. The current fixture pattern can leave behind the same kind of scratch tree and silently suppress cleanup failures.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29-34 and cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:56-61 call os.MkdirTemp with an empty root, change HOME, and discard os.RemoveAll errors. Changing HOME also changes the default GOPATH and GOMODCACHE for any Go subprocess or embedded tool that does not receive explicit values.

PROPOSED FIX
Replace the raw os.MkdirTemp fixtures with a shared test helper backed by t.TempDir so cleanup failures fail the test. Before changing HOME, preserve an explicit stable Go module-cache/GOPATH policy for child work so the isolated provider-config HOME cannot become a second module cache. Keep the LM Studio and OpenRouter embedded-dispatch tests using the helper and leave the no-real-provider/no-exec-path assertions intact.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production runner routing, make live provider calls, delete existing host scratch, or change production cleanup ownership/budgets. ddx-f914dddd and ddx-de1ff4b4 own those cleanup changes.

PARENT
ddx-6a2ce3bd.

DEPS
None.

In-scope files:
- cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go
- nearest internal/agent test helper if shared setup is warranted

1. `TestRunLMStudioDispatchesThroughEmbeddedAgent` continues to assert no real provider calls and no exec-path leakage while using the cleanup-checking HOME helper.
2. `TestRunOpenRouterDispatchesThroughEmbeddedAgent` continues to assert no real provider calls and no exec-path leakage while using the cleanup-checking HOME helper.
3. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run "Test(Run(LMStudio|OpenRouter)DispatchesThroughEmbeddedAgent)$" -count=1 -timeout 30s` passes.
4. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.

description:
PROBLEM
The live execute-bead path reaches ValidateAttemptIntegrity without the gate-run and implementation-command evidence needed to detect a provider that commits after a failed required gate or uses git commit --no-verify. That lets an invalid implementation attempt proceed toward merge/close instead of being preserved for operator review.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1507-1514 invokes ValidateAttemptIntegrity without GateRuns or implementation-command evidence. The nearest harness-session evidence adapter does not provide foreground gate command evidence, outputs, exit statuses, ordering relative to the final staged mutation and implementation commit, or implementation-agent git commands to this validation call.

PROPOSED FIX
Capture foreground gate commands, outputs, exit status, ordering relative to the final staged mutation and implementation commit, plus implementation-agent git commands from the harness session. Thread that evidence through the nearest execute-bead harness-session evidence adapter into ValidateAttemptIntegrity before landing. When the validator rejects the attempt, preserve the attempt with failure_mode=attempt_integrity rather than merging or closing it.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go
- nearest harness-session evidence adapter
- internal/agent execute-bead integrity tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not redesign the pure validation policy owned by ddx-c4497391. Do not rewrite existing execution history or forbid DDx-owned checkpoint, tracker-only, landing, or durable-audit commits. Do not change execute-bead prompt wording except where needed by the sibling prompt-guardrail bead.

PARENT
ddx-9c3e703b.

DEPS
ddx-c4497391.

acceptance:
1. TestAttemptCPUEnvelope_AppliesToProviderDescendants launches a real bounded helper whose harness root forks at least four CPU-busy descendants, including one that calls `setsid` and reparents, and proves the controller still contains the complete attempt tree with an effective default quota of 200 percent.
2. TestAttemptCPUEnvelope_ManualAndManagedParity runs the shared executor configuration through manual/offline and server-managed construction paths and proves requested/effective quota semantics are identical; the managed path still carries the existing parent-death behavior.
3. TestAttemptCPUEnvelope_DisabledIsExplicit proves a configured quota of 0 leaves the attempt unbounded and records that explicit policy rather than a controller failure.
4. TestAttemptCPUEnvelope_DegradedFallbackIsObservable proves an unavailable platform controller lowers scheduling priority, keeps the attempt runnable, and emits structured evidence with requested quota, effective mode, and fallback reason.
5. TestAttemptCPUEnvelope_CleanupRemovesController proves normal exit, timeout, cancellation, and provider-start failure do not leak controller state or descendants, including a session-changing/reparented tool child.
6. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/... ./cmd/... -run "TestAttemptCPUEnvelope_(AppliesToProviderDescendants|ManualAndManagedParity|DisabledIsExplicit|DegradedFallbackIsObservable|CleanupRemovesController)" -count=1 passes.
7. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/... ./cmd/... ./internal/integration/... passes.
8. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
A single DDx attempt can monopolize the entire server-owned CPU allowance. On 2026-07-13, TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace launched five Codex providers whose aggregate use reached about 350 percent CPU, nearly saturating the installed server CPUQuota=400 percent. The aggregate service cap protected the host but provided no fairness between attempts, and a manual/offline worker outside ddx-server.service has no equivalent cap at all.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/server_service.go:98-102 exposes only an aggregate CPU quota and weight for the complete server-owned worker/provider/build tree. cli/internal/service/service.go:15-22 defines that policy explicitly as aggregate. cli/internal/agent/executor.go:177-188 starts each provider directly, while cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:10-29 configures only a process group and parent-death signal; no attempt-scoped CPU controller contains the provider and all descendants. Consequently one nested test/provider fanout can consume the whole managed-service budget, while the same manual worker path is unbounded.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add one attempt-scoped CPU-envelope abstraction at the provider execution boundary so the harness root and every descendant share a bounded controller. Membership must survive process-group/session changes, double-forking, and reparenting; cleanup and cancellation must act on controller membership rather than ancestry alone.
- Apply the same default and configuration to server-managed and manual/offline workers without requiring a live DDx server. Preserve the existing parent-death behavior so managed provider trees still die when their worker/server dies.
- Use a conservative default of 200 percent of one core per active attempt, allow an explicit 0 value to disable the per-attempt cap, and keep the existing aggregate server service cap as the outer ceiling.
- Emit structured attempt evidence containing requested/effective quota, controller kind, descendant membership, and fallback reason. When the platform cannot enforce a hard quota, continue with lowered scheduling priority and an operator-visible degraded-control event rather than silently claiming enforcement.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/executor.go and adjacent platform-specific executor/resource-controller files
- cli/internal/config execution settings and validation
- cli/cmd/work.go and cli/cmd/try.go only for shared configuration plumbing
- cli/internal/integration for a real descendant-fanout proof

NON-SCOPE
Do not replace or remove the aggregate ddx-server.service CPUQuota/CPUWeight policy. Do not throttle arbitrary external cargo, Go, provider, or user processes that are not descendants of the current DDx attempt. Do not require the coordination server for manual/offline execution. Do not change desired worker count, queue ordering, provider routing, or the process-group/Pdeathsig ownership contract. ddx-aa6cc320 remains responsible for removing live providers from the default test fixture.
notes: Provider-descendant CPU containment belongs to the Fizeau harness/runtime boundary, not DDx attempt execution.

description:
PROBLEM: the Inter typeface is SPECIFIED but never LOADED. `cli/internal/server/frontend/design-tokens.json:20-39` declares `fontFamily.h1/h2/body-md/body-sm/label` as `["Inter"]`, and `cli/internal/server/frontend/tailwind.config.js:39-46` maps those into the `semanticFonts` aliases (`headline-lg`, `headline-md`, `body-md`, `body-sm`, `label-caps`). But there is no `@font-face` rule, no `@fontsource*` import, and no Google Fonts `<link>` anywhere in `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/app.css`, `src/app.html`, or `static/`. Confirmed: `grep -rn "font-face|fontsource|fonts.googleapis" src static` returns nothing, and `ls node_modules | grep -i fontsource` is empty. Every non-mono text role therefore renders the OS system-sans fallback (Segoe UI / Helvetica / DejaVu Sans depending on platform), not Inter — the metrics and weights in `.stitch/DESIGN.md` (`headline-lg` 800 weight, `label-caps` 700 with 0.05em tracking) are silently unmet, and screenshots differ per developer machine.

ROOT CAUSE: no font asset is imported by the frontend build. The Tailwind config names a family it never ships.

PROPOSED FIX: `cd cli/internal/server/frontend && bun add @fontsource-variable/inter`, then add `@import '@fontsource-variable/inter';` to `cli/internal/server/frontend/src/app.css` near the top, above the existing `@import 'tailwindcss';` at line 2 so the face is registered before Tailwind's layers. Update the family stacks so the loaded variable family is what the browser actually resolves: the family name shipped by that package is `'Inter Variable'`, so the `fontFamily` entries that currently read `["Inter"]` must include it (e.g. `['Inter Variable', 'Inter', 'system-ui', 'sans-serif']`), keeping a system fallback. Font family data lives in `design-tokens.json`; the alias layer at `tailwind.config.js:39-46` stays as-is. Commit the resulting `bun.lock` change.

NON-SCOPE: introducing a distinctive display font — the operator explicitly chose Inter-only, and adding a second family would be a spec change; the mono role (`mono-code`, `tailwind.config.js:45`) keeps its existing `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, JetBrains Mono, monospace` stack and no mono webfont is shipped; changing any color token (that is the sibling token-canonicalization bead); re-baselining Playwright screenshot snapshots (separate child bead — this bead must not run `--update-snapshots`); the Hugo website's fonts (`.stitch/PLAN.md` phase 5); any Go backend change.

description:
PROBLEM
During attempt 20260713T145533-c006900a, the model ran cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s, received the same host-scratch traversal failure, reran it after operator termination, and finally launched the equivalent suite through setsid -f with redirected output. The detached run entered a new session and continued consuming CPU/I/O until the operator killed it. The prompt explicitly prohibited an unchanged long-command replay, but DDx did not intervene.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2088-2094 expresses the command-fingerprint rule only as model instructions.
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:39-76 keys loop detection on tool name, raw input JSON, error text, and result output. The same expensive command with a different termination message, redirection, timeout wrapper, or setsid wrapper therefore produces a different key.
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:268-271 and 399-415 require four identical call-result pairs in an eight-entry window, so two or three costly replays can consume tens of minutes without firing.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:32-39 cannot reap a replay that changes session/process group; ddx-7df6b12a owns the attempt controller needed after cancellation.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an expensive-command replay detector over normalized service tool-call events. Canonicalize shell wrappers that do not change command semantics (cd into the same worktree, timeout, setsid, output redirection, foreground/background launch) while retaining command args, environment/config inputs, cwd, and a worktree/config fingerprint. After an expensive command fails, times out, or ends incomplete, cancel the attempt before a second equivalent replay unless the normalized args/environment/config or worktree fingerprint changed and the event records why the previous evidence is invalid. Persist a structured operator_attention event containing both fingerprints, outcomes, and the cancellation reason. Cancel through the ddx-7df6b12a attempt controller so detached/session-changing children are reaped.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go and adjacent replay-detector helpers/tests
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go for correlation/evidence plumbing
- attempt-controller integration introduced by ddx-7df6b12a
- execute-bead event/operator-attention mapping for replay cancellation

NON-SCOPE
Do not block distinct commands, cheap read-only commands, one legitimate validation after a code/config fingerprint change, or manual operator commands outside an attempt. Do not infer success from a killed or incomplete command. Do not lower the generic four-pair loop detector for non-expensive tools.

PARENT AND DEPS
Root reliability incident. Depends on ddx-7df6b12a for controller-backed cancellation. Related to ddx-45ea2e36, which owns the independent hard attempt deadline.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx repeatedly decomposes already-narrow work into more child layers, so queue activity can increase faster than fixes land. In the live Niflheim queue, representative chains reached `niflheim-8c7428de -> niflheim-515a7439 -> niflheim-b476f419 -> niflheim-34c8eb2e/niflheim-6cfc6148` and `niflheim-4093e6df -> niflheim-586e9520 -> niflheim-10932cf3 -> niflheim-e3a5db27/niflheim-e076a89c`. During one 39-minute observation window only one bead closed while open work grew from 130 to 137 and ready work grew from 73 to 77. Claims, retries, and decomposition were reported as progress despite negative net queue throughput.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/config/types.go:482-501` gives queue triage its own `MaxDecompositionDepth`, defaulting to three generated levels.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2462-2483` separately tells implementation agents there is a hard cap of two generated levels and says not to create another child layer at that cap.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_intake_decompose_test.go:534-612` explicitly preserves the disagreement: `TestPostAttemptTooLargeNoChanges_UsesQueueDepthNotAttemptPromptDepth` expects the queue default/configured depth of three to override the implementation prompt cap of two and create another child.
- The decision path checks depth but has no family-wide expansion budget and no requirement that each split materially reduce implementation complexity. An already-decomposed, actionable bead can therefore be split again, including into verification-shaped children, while the queue grows.

PROPOSED FIX
Use one resolved decomposition-depth policy across preclaim intake, post-attempt recovery, prompts, and configuration, with a conservative default no greater than two generated child levels. Before creating children, require evidence that the parent contains independent implementation boundaries, that every child owns a concrete implementation outcome and acceptance mapping, and that the split materially reduces complexity rather than moving validation or bookkeeping into separate beads. Add a bounded descendant/expansion budget for the entire bead family. At the depth or expansion cap, execute an actionable atomic child or park the bead once with a reason; do not create another layer. Emit structured telemetry for family size, depth, split reason, and refusal reason so operators can distinguish landed progress from queue expansion.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not prohibit legitimate epic decomposition or independent parallel deliverables.
- Do not weaken acceptance validation or readiness checks.
- Do not change model routing or retry policy except where it currently triggers another decomposition layer.
- Do not rewrite the existing Niflheim tracker.
- Malformed deterministic fallback children remain owned by `ddx-6ded197d`; preclaim lifecycle process reaping remains owned by `ddx-092f0d34`.

description:
PROBLEM
The normal internal/agent gate timed out after 10 minutes while TestLifecycleDispatchRejectsProjectRootMutation waited for captureLifecycleProjectStatus. One unbounded project-status subprocess can consume the complete package budget, fail unrelated beads, and force the queue to retry work whose focused acceptance tests are already green.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go:95-117 accepts no context. At line 105 it calls RepairKnownConfigCorruption with context.Background, and at line 110 it runs git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all with context.Background. The before, after, and restored snapshots at cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go:47, 144, and 157 therefore outlive caller cancellation and have no per-operation deadline. In attempt 20260713T104022-f6d5cb82, the package timeout stack showed TestLifecycleDispatchRejectsProjectRootMutation blocked in internalgit.Command(... status ...).CombinedOutput at lifecycle_dispatch.go:110.

PROPOSED FIX
Thread the lifecycle dispatch caller context through every project-status snapshot and repository-health repair. Derive a short per-snapshot deadline, capped by the caller deadline, and ensure cancellation terminates and waits for the Git subprocess. Return a typed lifecycle snapshot error that preserves deadline/cancellation diagnostics so the intake hook fails promptly instead of holding the package gate.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go
- cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook_test.go or a focused lifecycle dispatch test file
- nearest internal Git test helper only if needed for a blocking git shim

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken project-root mutation detection, skip pre/post/restored snapshots, change queue retry policy, increase the package timeout, or alter unrelated Git locking and tracker serialization. Do not rerun or close ddx-69672921 in this bead.

PARENT
None; root lifecycle reliability regression.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
When several `ddx try` / `ddx work` attempts run concurrently against one project, an attempt can abort with `execution_failed` before doing any work, because its pre-execute-bead checkpoint tries to stage a file that a sibling process deleted microseconds earlier.

Observed (2026-07-21, internal/integration under -race load):
  pre-execute-bead checkpoint: staging checkpoint changes:
  fatal: pathspec '.ddx/executions/.ddx-resource-preflight-1822793358' did not match any files: exit status 128
The whole attempt was reported execution_failed even though nothing was wrong with the bead.

ROOT CAUSE
The checkpoint enumerates dirty paths and then passes that list to `git add` as explicit pathspecs. Between the enumeration and the `git add`, a sibling attempt's resource-preflight temp file under `.ddx/executions/` is removed, so the pathspec no longer matches and git exits 128. This is a time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap: the path list is a snapshot, but `git add` requires every pathspec to still resolve.

The staging call lives in the pre-dispatch checkpoint path in cli/internal/agent/ (search: "staging checkpoint changes"). Two things are wrong:
1. `.ddx/executions/` is per-machine working state (see CLAUDE.md, "Execution Evidence Convention") and is gitignored; it should never be enumerated as checkpoint-worthy dirt in the first place.
2. Even for legitimate paths, `git add` with explicit pathspecs must tolerate a path vanishing under it.

PROPOSED FIX
- Exclude `.ddx/executions/**` from the pre-dispatch checkpoint's dirty enumeration, the same way cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:489 already excludes `.ddx/beads.lock.*.lock` as runtime coordination state.
- Pass `--ignore-missing` semantics or re-filter the pathspec list immediately before `git add`, so a concurrently-deleted path degrades to a skipped file rather than a failed attempt.
- Classify a residual `did not match any files` staging error as retryable rather than execution_failed.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change what the checkpoint commits for legitimately dirty tracked files.
- Do not address the land-time compare-and-swap loss (sister bead) or the dirty-worktree guard's sibling-output sensitivity (sister bead).

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can leave normative requirements unmapped, map the same requirement more than once, or carry no verification evidence at all while still passing lint. FEAT-009/FEAT-002/FEAT-012 are called out by the Phase 2 recovery plan as Complete documents with absent or incomplete verification coverage.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The requested spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the parent analyzer work has not yet added Complete-status verification-coverage logic. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, which requires every Complete/Implemented requirement or stable anchor to be covered exactly once by a Verification mapping row, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, which requires uncovered and duplicate mappings to fail.

PROPOSED FIX
After the scaffold/status-parser child and Verification mapping-parser child provide the Complete/Implemented document set, requirement inventory, and mapping rows model, add the coverage-cardinality pass: for every Complete/Implemented document, require at least one verification row, require every inventory requirement/anchor to be covered by exactly one row, emit one diagnostic per uncovered requirement, and emit one diagnostic per duplicate mapping. Treat a test-file path without the exact mapped test/check/artifact target as non-coverage for this cardinality pass. Analyzer remains read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts exist — evidence-target resolution is a sibling child. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist — command allowlist enforcement is a sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
The legacy Runner embedded-provider path cannot be isolated with the package test factory. Tests that only need to prove lmstudio/openrouter dispatch reaches RunAgent instead construct a real Fizeau service, start discovery/background state work, and race t.TempDir cleanup. Attempt 20260713T114250-0509adf3 repeatedly failed cleanup with late files under HOME/.cache/fizeau and XDG_DATA_HOME/ddx/projects/local until it patched the production seam.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:112-123 calls NewServiceFromWorkDir directly inside runAgentViaService.
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:22-80 defines SetServiceRunFactory and resolveService specifically so internal callers honor a hermetic test service while production falls back to NewServiceFromWorkDir. RunWithConfigViaService uses that resolver, but the legacy RunAgent path bypasses it.

PROPOSED FIX
- Change runAgentViaService in cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go to obtain its service through resolveService(wd), preserving the nil-factory production fallback.
- Add TestRunAgentViaService_HonorsServiceRunFactory in cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service_test.go. Install a passthroughTestService factory, record the supplied workdir/request, invoke the legacy RunAgent path, and restore the global factory with t.Cleanup.
- Keep the factory override test-only; do not introduce a production configuration path or alter route/provider selection.

NON-SCOPE
Do not refactor the HOME/XDG fixture itself; child/consumer bead ddx-7326dd54 owns that. Do not change Fizeau discovery cancellation or process reaping; ddx-a751a7b1 and ddx-93d8b7c8 own those fixes. Do not add ignored RemoveAll cleanup.

PARENT
ddx-7326dd54.

DEPS
No deps.

description:
PROBLEM: `cli/internal/server/frontend/design-tokens.json` is the STALE generic Stitch export. Its values are the placeholder palette — `primary:#4878c6` (line 5), `secondary:#35a35f` (line 6), `tertiary:#8e35a3` purple (line 7), `background:#ffffff` (line 8), `surface:#f9fafb` (line 9), `text:#111827` (line 11), `terminal-bg:#0f1117` (line 17), `terminal-fg:#e8eaf0` (line 18) — none of which are the warm-paper brutalist palette specified in `.stitch/DESIGN.md`. The intended warm values only reach the running app because `cli/internal/server/frontend/tailwind.config.js:8-37` hardcodes a `semanticColors` block that overrides several of them (`accent-lever:'#3B5B7A'` line 9, `bg-canvas:'#F4EFE6'` line 16, `border-line:'#E4DDD0'` line 28, all `dark-*` entries). The remaining aliases still read straight through to generic data: `accent-fulcrum: colors.secondary` (line 10) resolves to green `#35a35f` instead of Iron Gray `#3F4147`; `accent-load: colors.tertiary` (line 11) resolves to purple `#8e35a3` instead of Aged Brass `#A8801F`; `bg-surface: colors.surface` (line 17) resolves to `#f9fafb` instead of Parchment `#FBF8F2`; `bg-elevated: colors.background` (line 18) resolves via generic `#ffffff`; `fg-ink: colors.text` (line 23) resolves to `#111827` instead of `#1F2125`; `terminal-bg`/`terminal-fg` (lines 31, 33) resolve to the cool `#0f1117`/`#e8eaf0` instead of `#1F2125`/`#D8D2C4`.

ROOT CAUSE: the token export pipeline — `package.json:12` at the repo root, `"design:export": "bunx @google/design.md export --format tailwind .stitch/DESIGN.md > cli/internal/server/frontend/design-tokens.json"` — has not been re-run against the current `.stitch/DESIGN.md`, so the committed JSON still carries generic default DATA. Re-running it today would regenerate generic values, and a reader cannot tell whether the JSON or the hardcoded `semanticColors` block is authoritative. acceptance:
1. `TestBeadQueueTopPrecedesExistingRankZero` seeds an older rank-zero bead, tops a newer bead, and proves the topped bead has a strictly lower numeric rank and is first in ReadyExecution order.
2. `TestOpsQueue_TopRepeatedCallsStrictlyReorder` tops at least three beads successively and proves each most-recent target becomes uniquely first with deterministic ordering of prior targets.
3. `TestBeadQueueTopPreservesOtherPriorityBucket` proves top leaves every rank and row in an unrelated priority bucket unchanged.
4. `cd cli && go test ./cmd/... ./internal/bead/ops/queue/... -run '^(TestBeadQueueTop(PrecedesExistingRankZero|PreservesOtherPriorityBucket)|TestOpsQueue_TopRepeatedCallsStrictlyReorder)$' -count=1` passes.
5. `cd cli && go test ./cmd/... ./internal/bead/...` passes.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
During the 2026-07-13 Niflheim queue drain, the operator ran `ddx bead queue top` on four newly discovered P0 reliability beads. Each command succeeded and committed, but all four beads received `queue-rank: 0`; `ddx bead ready` continued to put the older retry bead `ddx-415c8b95` first. The command therefore does not fulfill “move to the front” once any bead in the priority bucket already has rank zero.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/bead/ops/queue/queue.go:25-32` implements `Top` as a direct `QueueSetTop{}` mutation without reading the priority bucket.
- `cli/internal/bead/operation.go:8-17` hard-codes every `QueueSetTop` result to rank zero.
- `cli/internal/bead/ops/queue/queue.go:34-75` already has the correct bucket-aware `Move(..., position=0)` machinery, including sparse negative ranks and renormalization, but `Top` bypasses it.
- `cli/cmd/bead_queue_test.go:48-71` tests top only against unranked beads and misses existing-rank-zero and repeated-top cases.
This regresses the ordering semantics specified and previously closed by `ddx-d0c656b0`.

PROPOSED FIX
Make `Top` use the same bucket-aware positioning contract as `Move` so the target strictly sorts before the current first bead, including when one or many entries already have rank zero. Preserve priority and avoid rewriting unrelated priority buckets. Add command- and ops-level repeated-top coverage.

NON-SCOPE
Changing priority values, global cross-priority ordering, clearing operator ranks, changing ready eligibility, or manually editing tracker JSONL.

PARENT
None; root queue-ordering regression found while prioritizing Niflheim reliability work.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

description:
PROBLEM
When several attempts share one project worktree, the pre-dispatch dirty-worktree guard sees a sibling attempt's in-flight output file, concludes the operator has uncommitted work, and releases a perfectly healthy claim:
  operator attention: project worktree ... has uncommitted implementation changes;
  released ddxfixture-c16c024e ... out-ddxfixture-b70d1d65.txt
Note the released bead (c16c024e) and the file that triggered it (b70d1d65) belong to DIFFERENT beads. The guard is attributing a sibling's work to the current attempt.

Observed 2026-07-21 in internal/integration concurrent-try load testing.

ROOT CAUSE
The guard in cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go treats any unignored dirt in the project worktree as operator work. It already special-cases runtime coordination state (`.ddx/beads.lock.*.lock`, predispatch_dirty.go:489) but has no notion of "this path belongs to another live attempt". Under concurrency the guard is not attempt-aware, so a sibling's output file is indistinguishable from an operator edit — and the conservative response (release the claim, raise operator attention) is exactly wrong.

PROPOSED FIX
- Make the guard attempt-aware: paths owned by another live attempt (identifiable from the running-attempt registry / claim leases, or by the `out-<beadID>` naming the fixtures use) must not count as operator dirt for a different bead.
- Where ownership cannot be established, prefer blocking only the attempt whose own worktree is dirty rather than releasing the claim.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not weaken the guard for genuine operator edits; an uncommitted change with no live-attempt owner must still raise operator attention.
- Do not address the checkpoint staging TOCTOU or the tracker lost-update (sister beads).

acceptance:

2. TestOwnedScratchMarkerRoundTrip (or a sibling assertion within it) proves a missing or malformed marker yields an uncertain/unowned status rather than an ownership claim, consistent with ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/scratchowner/... -run "TestOwnedScratchMarkerRoundTrip$" -count=1 passes.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/scratchowner/... passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
There is no lower-level contract that a producer of process-lifetime scratch directories can use to record durable ownership evidence, and that execution cleanup can read, without creating an import cycle between internal/testutils and internal/agent. Without this marker, a directory's name prefix plus age becomes the only signal available to cleanup, which cannot distinguish an abandoned directory from one still owned by a live long-running test process.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:119-167 creates and publishes binary directories with no durable owner marker, so there is nothing for cleanup to key ownership on.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:667-681 synthesizes ownership only when cleanup.json is absent, and cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:189-221 preserves a directory with live PID or lease evidence only when compatible metadata already exists — no shared marker type exists that both a testutils producer and the agent cleaner can construct and validate.
ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 establish host-global trust and metadata-marked reclamation rules but define no producer-writable process-lifetime ownership marker.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a small internal/scratchowner package that defines an owner-marker contract importable by both internal/testutils and internal/agent with no import cycle. The marker records: resource kind, owner PID, creation time, and a process-start identity when the platform exposes one. Provide atomic write (temp file + rename within the target directory) and a read/validate path that reports live, dead, or uncertain owner status consistent with the ownership rules in ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93. A prefix or name match is never treated as ownership proof.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- a new cli/internal/scratchowner package and its tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not modify fixture_repo.go producers or execution_cleanup.go in this bead; child beads ddx (fixture producers) and ddx (cleanup wiring) consume this contract.
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not redesign general host-global scratch trust; ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 own that policy.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
ddx-1eb1ba93 must land first so metadata-marked reclamation and host-global ownership rules are established; it already depends on ddx-05e3d16b.

description:
PROBLEM
The server cannot be demoted to observer mode because managed workers can still spawn from multiple command and supervisor entry points.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/server/workers_supervisor.go:290-301 and cli/cmd/worker.go:96-113 allow managed spawn/enable without one server.manage_workers gate. Phase 3 WB-1 requires spawn-side demotion at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:94-102.

PROPOSED FIX
Add one configuration authority for server-managed DDx worker spawning, default it disabled during the rebuild, reject enable/start mutations with a typed management_disabled result, and zero desired managed state on disable. Preserve observer ingestion and repair.

NON-SCOPE
Do not stop manual ddx work, disable observer repair, kill provider processes, or change Fizeau routing.

PARENT
ddx-61c41896.

DEPS
Phase 0 exit before enabling implementation; bead may remain waiting until then.

description:
PROBLEM
A watch worker can prove its temp/evidence roots are healthy on every dispatch, yet beads previously blocked by local resource exhaustion remain outside candidate selection forever. This required manually reopening fifteen beads after the July 11 ENOSPC incident.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2352-2363 performs an idle-path auto-reopen only for retryable provider-connectivity proposals before nextCandidate. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2492-2576 reports and sleeps on no ready work without rechecking blocked local resources. cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:208-300 already supplies the authoritative root health probe, but the idle lifecycle path never applies it to typed blocked beads.

PROPOSED FIX
- Before candidate selection in watch mode, list blocked beads carrying the typed local_resource_exhaustion marker from ddx-c4cbf253.
- Run the configured ExecutionResourceChecker once per idle pass. Reopen all matching beads through LifecycleTransitionOptions{ManualReopen:true} only when the probe is healthy.
- Append durable local_resource_blocker_recheck evidence containing before/after root checks and emit a loop event.
- Leave typed blockers blocked when the probe is unhealthy and leave every untyped/manual blocker untouched.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_resource_exhausted_test.go or one focused companion test

NON-SCOPE
- Do not parse free-text blocker reasons.
- Do not reopen cross-repo, provider, test-suite, or operator-decision blockers.
- Do not change resource thresholds or cleanup policy.

PARENT
- ddx-5958e8a4.

DEPS
- ddx-c4cbf253 persists the typed marker.
