description:
PROBLEM
With the slot pool, reuse/scrub path, and preserved build state implemented in the sibling children, the production execute-bead path still prepares a throwaway workspace per attempt and defers destructive cleanup, so no real bead benefits and operators have no visibility into whether reuse is happening or what it saves.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares a workspace with `attemptBackend.Prepare(...)` for every attempt and installs a `defer` that ends in `_ = attemptBackend.Cleanup(ctx, workspace)`, treating the workspace as disposable; the only preservation branch is `runtime.PreserveAttemptWorktree` for the worktree backend.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031` (`WriteExecutionCleanupMetadata`) writes per-attempt metadata into the workspace, which must be scrubbed on reuse rather than carried into the next bead.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) constructs backends without any pool handle or worker-slot identity, so orchestration has nothing to thread through.
- No hit/miss or savings counters exist anywhere in the attempt path, so there is no signal that would have surfaced the Niflheim cold-build amplification (roughly 20-24 minutes per bead in cold lefthook/clippy runs).

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Thread the resolved reusable-workspace policy and worker-slot identity from `ResolveAttemptBackend` into both the linked-worktree and local-clone backends so production preparation goes through the bounded slot allocator. Replace the unconditional destructive cleanup in the `execute_bead.go` defer with a release that returns a healthy slot to the pool and only deletes on quarantine, while preserving existing `PreserveAttemptWorktree`, `KeepOnError`, evidence-preservation, and the `resource_exhausted` classification of `Prepare` failures. Emit reuse telemetry — slot hit/miss counts plus time and bytes saved — through the existing execution event/observability path so operators can see reuse behaviour per project and worker.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
When an operator reviews a preserved dangling-success result and rejects it (bad implementation), the bead is set back to open for a fresh attempt. But on the next drain pass, a worker sees the still-existing preserved result ref, re-preserves it, and re-proposes the bead for operator landing — an endless propose/reject loop. Observed 3x on 2026-07-23 with ddx-074a82c2: its preserved result 3e787d9eb4 was operator-rejected (hard-coded example path as policy — see that bead's notes), reset to open at ~05:00, and re-proposed by workers at ~12:5x and ~17:2x without any fresh implementation attempt.

ROOT CAUSE
The dangling-success re-preserve path (emitter of dangling-success-preserved events in cli/internal/agent) treats any preserved result ref for an open bead as landable and re-proposes, with no record that an operator already rejected that specific result_rev.

PROPOSED FIX
Record operator rejection as a structured bead event (e.g. kind=preserved-result-rejected with the rejected result_rev). Before re-proposing a preserved result, the worker checks for a rejection event matching that result_rev; if rejected, skip the preserve/propose and treat the bead as ordinary ready work (fresh attempt). Provide the rejection via a CLI surface (e.g. ddx bead update <id> --reject-preserved <rev> or an event-append command) so operators do not hand-edit events.

NON-SCOPE
Automatic deletion of preserve refs (audit trail stays); changing dangling-success detection for non-rejected results.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still chooses or biases concrete Fizeau routes in production even after removing the obvious run/try/work preflight. Local harness-name dispatch, lifecycle profile discovery, server defaults, project-model inheritance, and dead exported route-control APIs let DDx select harness/provider/model/profile policy it does not own. Removing preflight also left the advertised 60s route-resolution lease guard disconnected.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:90-135, cli/internal/agent/dispatch.go:36-67, and cli/internal/agent/runner.go:84-114 route virtual/script names into DDx-local runners instead of forwarding an operator harness constraint to Fizeau.
- cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:477-494,559-579 and cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:237-247 call ListPolicies/ListModels and select concrete lifecycle profiles.
- cli/internal/server/graphql_adapters.go:73-100, workers_supervisor.go:23-106, graphql/resolver_feat008.go:89-120, and the workers frontend seed default/smart profiles; server workers.go:363-372 and agent/run_dispatch_spec.go:103-127 leave opaque passthrough false, so config/resolved.go:73-80 can inject project agent.model into an unpinned request.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6935-7533, service_run.go:461-636, cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_escalation.go:104-379, internal/agent/escalation/ladder.go, and model_discovery_containment.go retain exclusion, resolver, catalog-ladder, historical-route-seeding, and discovery-control capabilities.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:88-91,215-228 plus work/try/server flag plumbing retain route-resolution-timeout after deleting its resolver call, making the documented lease-release guard a no-op.

PROPOSED FIX
Route every production agent and lifecycle invocation through Fizeau. Preserve explicit operator Harness, Provider, Model, Policy/Profile, MaxPower, and other public passthrough byte-for-byte, but never synthesize concrete route fields. Express DDx-owned difficulty or escalation only through abstract MinPower. Remove local script/virtual name dispatch from production, lifecycle catalog/profile selection, default/smart profile injection, project-model inheritance for opaque execution entry points, route exclusion/catalog/seed machinery, and dead exported control APIs. Retain the 60s wedge guard by timing only Fizeau's opaque route stage from Execute dispatch until its first routing_decision event; on expiry cancel the operation, release the lease, and append operator_attention, and permanently disarm the timer once routing_decision arrives.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove read-only provider/model inventory or UI display of Fizeau-returned route evidence, change Fizeau internals, reject explicit operator passthrough, implement typed-result policy that requires a newer Fizeau release, or implement reviewer cardinality/stronger-review policy owned by dependent beads.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
None; Phase 1 WB-2a is start-immediately and this bead is the execution-boundary prerequisite for difficulty and review work.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can leave normative requirements unmapped or map the same requirement more than once and still pass lint. An unmapped requirement means a Complete stamp covers work with no stated proof; a duplicated mapping hides which row is the authoritative evidence and inflates apparent coverage.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout — the expected path cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent (cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, runtimelint). No pass performs coverage-cardinality arithmetic between a document's requirement inventory and its Verification mapping rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67 (every Complete/Implemented requirement or stable anchor covered exactly once) and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68 (uncovered and duplicate mappings must fail).

PROPOSED FIX
Consuming the Complete/Implemented document set from the scaffold/status-parser child and the requirement inventory plus mapping-rows model from the Verification mapping-parser child, add the coverage-cardinality pass: for each Complete/Implemented document, join inventory requirements/anchors against mapping rows by requirement identifier, emit one diagnostic per requirement covered zero times naming that requirement, and emit one diagnostic per requirement covered more than once naming that requirement as a duplicate mapping. A requirement covered exactly once yields no diagnostic. Follow the package and test conventions in cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the zero-evidence (empty row set) diagnostic — that is the sibling zero-evidence child. Do not implement the file-only-citation exclusion rule — that is the sibling citation-granularity child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child; consume its model. Do not implement status parsing — that is the scaffold child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts exist — evidence-target resolution is a sibling child. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist — command allowlist enforcement is a sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5 (and its parent ddx-471d66b6); the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-8a78ee90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestExecuteBeadPrompt_UsesImplementationCommitAsSinglePreCommitGate` proves both rich and embedded prompts tell the agent to stage exact paths and rely on the normal commit hook once, without requesting a separate identical staged `lefthook` run.

description:
PROBLEM
Attempt 20260713T094206-53684645 for ddx-415c8b95 had a staged pre-commit gate terminated after it recursively walked 100 leaked host-global module caches. The provider then ran git commit --no-verify and DDx accepted, merged, closed, and pushed implementation commit 85bb0fae0. A code-changing attempt can therefore bypass its required staged hook and still be classified as successful.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2108-2113 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2143-2148 require tests and a staged lefthook run but do not explicitly forbid --no-verify, hook disabling, or bypassing a failed gate. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1507-1514 invokes ValidateAttemptIntegrity without populating GateRuns. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go:160-186 checks gate evidence only when len(GateRuns) is nonzero, and TestValidateAttemptIntegrity_SingleCommitNoEvidenceSkips codifies missing evidence as success. The validation promised by closed bead ddx-725b65b4 is therefore not wired into the live execute-bead path.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add an explicit execute-bead instruction that implementation agents must never use git commit --no-verify, disable hooks, or commit after a required gate failed or was interrupted.
- Capture implementation-agent tool commands and foreground gate outputs/exit codes from the harness session into structured attempt-integrity input.
- When a code-changing bead acceptance requires lefthook run pre-commit, require at least one successful meaningful staged run after the final staged mutation and before the implementation commit. Missing, failed, interrupted, background-only, or no-staged-files evidence must reject and preserve the attempt.
- Treat an implementation-agent git commit --no-verify command as an integrity violation even if a prior gate appeared meaningful.
- Keep DDx-owned checkpoint, tracker-only, landing, and durable-audit commits outside this rule; their scoped --no-verify use is orchestrator-owned.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation_test.go
- execute-bead prompt guardrail/snapshot tests
- nearest harness-session evidence adapter needed to populate GateRuns and implementation commands

NON-SCOPE
Do not rewrite or remove existing execute-bead history, forbid DDx-owned tracker/audit commits, rerun repository hooks for synthesized commits, or weaken required gates. ddx-a3358532 owns synthesized-commit hook behavior.

PARENT
None; root attempt-integrity regression.

DEPS
Related to closed ddx-725b65b4 and open ddx-2295d9b1, but no dependency is required.

description:
PROBLEM
On Rust queues every worker rebuilds a large dependency graph into a separate per-attempt target directory. In the live Niflheim queue this made otherwise bounded documentation and code beads spend roughly 20-24 minutes in cold lefthook/clippy runs while concurrent workers rebuilt jemalloc, aws-lc, and rdkafka and contended on Cargo locks. A reusable workspace slot alone does not fix this: DDx must explicitly preserve an allowlisted per-slot Cargo target directory and package caches, keep those caches distinct per concurrent worker, and invalidate them when the toolchain or dependency lock changes.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:568-577` (`dockerSharedCacheRoot`, `dockerSharedGoCachePath`) is the only cross-attempt build-cache persistence in DDx, it is Go-only, and it is consumed only by the Docker path at `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:289` and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:877-878`. Linked-worktree and local-clone attempts get no reusable build state at all.
- Because `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:199-233` recreates the clone per attempt and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` deletes it, any `target/` produced by a bead is destroyed on cleanup, guaranteeing a cold Cargo build next time.
- `cli/internal/config/types.go:348-364` (`ExecutionsConfig`) has no language build-cache policy, so there is no supported way to declare which build state is safe to keep.
- No code compares a preserved cache against the active Rust toolchain or dependency lock, so a naively-preserved `target/` would be reused across incompatible toolchains.

PROPOSED FIX
Build on the slot allocator and the reuse/scrub path from the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface" and "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine" (DEPENDS ON both). Generalize the Docker-only shared cache into a per-slot allowlisted build-state area covering a Cargo target directory and Cargo package/registry caches, keyed so that each concurrent worker slot gets its own mutable target and two workers can never lock the same one. Add the build-cache policy to `ExecutionsConfig`. Record a cache fingerprint covering the Rust toolchain identity and the dependency lock; on mismatch, invalidate the preserved build state safely without leaking workspace or source state and without corrupting the slot. Source-tree correctness and base-revision correctness from the scrub path must be preserved: only allowlisted build directories survive.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement the slot pool, scrub, or quarantine logic (sibling children).
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry (sibling child).

description:
PROBLEM
After an execution provider exits with task_failed and leaves implementation edits, DDx synthesizes an iteration commit. That commit runs the repository pre-commit hook even though the provider already ran or failed the same gate. On 2026-07-13, the failed ddx-0f29e87a attempt entered the internal/agent race suite a second time during synthesis and recreated real Codex provider processes, consuming CPU and preventing prompt failure finalization.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1297-1383 invokes GitOps.SynthesizeCommit whenever the attempt worktree is dirty and HEAD did not move, including when exitCode is non-zero and the preliminary outcome is task_failed. cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:151-180 stages the implementation diff and executes plain git commit -m, so repository hooks run inside DDx orchestration. The durable DDx audit paths already use --no-verify at cli/internal/agent/durable_audit.go:125-128 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1724-1731, demonstrating the intended separation between orchestration-owned commits and user-invoked validation.

PROPOSED FIX
Make RealGitOps.SynthesizeCommit create the DDx-owned synthesized attempt commit without invoking repository hooks. Preserve the substantive dirty diff and the per-attempt commit-message/audit contract. Keep validation in the provider run and DDx gate/review pipeline; do not silently reinterpret a failed attempt as success.

NON-SCOPE
Do not skip provider-requested gates, landing gates, or operator git hooks. Do not discard failed implementation edits or rewrite existing execute-bead history. Do not weaken test assertions or timeouts.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx estimates missing cost from concrete model and harness identity, accepts its own local price input, and stores execution cost in a value-only field. PROBLEM
DDx currently guesses that reviewer errors are transport failures from error strings, raises reviewer power/profile on retry, and ultimately fails or parks otherwise valid implementation work. Consume the single typed Fizeau terminal review-transport cause from the DDx attempt-policy adapter. Retry exactly once at identical MinPower and byte-identical operator passthrough. If the typed transport failure repeats, emit an operator-visible review-downgraded event and allow deterministic-checks-only close. Do not raise power, select a profile, or fail the implementation because review transport is unavailable. Non-transport review errors remain distinct and follow their typed policy.

1. TestCallerMigration_AgentAndServerUseInterfaces passes and AST-scans cli/internal/agent/, cli/internal/agent/try/, cli/internal/server/, cli/internal/server/graphql/, and cli/internal/escalation/ for concrete *bead.Store field/local usage outside documented construction/test-fixture exceptions.
2. TestServerStoresUseBackendInterfaces passes and verifies server/GraphQL resolver seams expose bead.Backend, bead.ReadOnlyBackend, or narrower interfaces rather than *bead.Store.
3. TestExecuteBeadLoopStoreDoesNotExposeConcreteStore passes and proves execute-loop dependencies can be satisfied without naming *bead.Store outside test construction helpers.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/server/... ./internal/escalation/... passes.

description:
PROBLEM
TD-027 §21 requires the agent and server layers to compile against bead interface contracts before storage concretes are relocated. These packages still have many *bead.Store test fixtures, helper wrappers, and production escape hatches that make the later internal-package move too broad and fragile.

ROOT CAUSE with file:line
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:1580 accepts *bead.Store in staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/ddxroot_paths.go:12 returns *bead.Store from projectBeadStore.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_mutation_beads.go:14 returns *bead.Store from mutationResolver.beadStore.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_integration_test.go:199 type-asserts a store back to *bead.Store.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:5896 documents deterministic ready-queue eligibility as bead.Store-specific instead of depending on an interface.
- Many agent/server test helpers still return *bead.Store, which prevents a package-level AST proof from staying small.

PROPOSED FIX
Update agent, agent/try, server, and server/graphql production code and test helpers to accept bead.Backend, bead.ReadOnlyBackend, or existing narrow sub-interfaces where the concrete is not required. Introduce local test-only fakes/adapters where a test currently embeds *bead.Store only to satisfy a small method set. Preserve concrete construction only at the package boundary where NewStore/NewStoreWithCollection is called.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change command/metrics caller clusters assigned to the sibling caller-narrowing child.
- Do not move storage concrete definitions or aliases.
- Do not relocate lifecycle WatcherHub.
- Do not change queue semantics, claim semantics, retry policy, worker lifecycle policy, or GraphQL behavior except for type narrowing.
- Do not implement per-concern L/C/X/Q/D/A/MIG behavior or AxonStore/AxonBackend behavior.
- Do not manually edit .ddx/beads.jsonl.
- Do not fix unrelated provider-launch/orphan integration flakes; if cd cli && go test ./... is blocked by pre-existing failures, report exact failing Test* names and leave this child’s changes otherwise verified.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
- TD-027 §21 Module Boundary / Boundary Lockdown.

PARENT/DEPS
- Parent: ddx-74452926.
- Must be scheduled after foundation ddx-c6317784 and the per-concern dependency beads already referenced by the parent, including ddx-3af1c1a6, ddx-71d3a2de, ddx-0ab16765, and Axon follow-up ddx-9c5bca8f where applicable.

description: PROBLEM: on 2026-07-06..2026-07-19 two ddx drains of telepathdata/cayce silently forked the repo: one checkout had branch.master.merge=refs/heads/main while the repo default was refs/heads/master, so each worker fleet pushed commits AND the beads.jsonl tracker to a different remote branch for 13 days. Because the tracker lives in git, forking the branch forks the queue itself — both sides showed healthy progress, duplicated ~100 non-chore commits of work under different bead IDs, and nobody was alerted. Recovered manually on 2026-07-20 (archive branch + delete + port-audit bead cayce-30ea87db). ROOT CAUSE: ddx work/try honor whatever upstream the checkout is configured with and have no preflight check that the branch being drained is (or descends from) the remote's default branch (origin/HEAD). PROPOSED FIX: before claiming the first bead, ddx work (and ddx try) resolve origin/HEAD and compare with the current branch's upstream: hard-fail with a clear message when the upstream ref names a different branch than origin/HEAD (override flag, e.g. --allow-non-default-branch, for deliberate feature-branch drains); also warn when the local branch is behind its upstream at drain start. Same check surfaced in ddx doctor.

2. TestLefthookGoTest_FromCliRootRemainsCompatible invokes the helper from cli/ with internal/agent/example.go and proves the same package command runs exactly once.
3. TestLefthookGoTest_UnmappedGoPathFailsClosed supplies an unmappable Go path and proves the helper exits nonzero with a diagnostic that names the rejected path.
4. TestLefthookGoTest_DeduplicatesPackageSelection supplies multiple Go files in one package and proves the package is tested once.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "^(TestLefthookGoTest_(FromRepoRootRunsInternalAgent|FromCliRootRemainsCompatible|UnmappedGoPathFailsClosed|DeduplicatesPackageSelection))$" -count=1 -timeout 60s passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
The targeted Go pre-commit helper can report success without running any tests when it is invoked from the repository root with the same root-relative cli/... paths that Git and operator diagnostics naturally produce. During execute-bead attempt 20260713T171608-d879ec96, sh scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go returned 0 in 123ms and launched no go process, creating false validation evidence after the real package gate had timed out.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh:8-18 converts each input to a directory, strips a leading cli/, and silently continues when that derived directory does not exist relative to the current working directory. lefthook.yml:11-14 and lefthook.yml:205-216 normally run the helper with cli/ as the command root, but the helper neither establishes nor validates that working-directory contract. From the repository root, cli/internal/agent becomes internal/agent, the directory check fails, and the helper exits with its initial zero status.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the helper resolve the Go module root deterministically from its own repository location or explicitly normalize both repository-root cli/... paths and cli-root internal/... paths before selecting packages. Track every Go path supplied to the helper and fail nonzero with a diagnostic naming any path that cannot be mapped to an existing module package. Preserve targeted package selection, the race detector, the 30-minute per-package timeout, and compatibility with the normal Lefthook cli/ root.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh
- lefthook.yml only if invocation wiring needs an explicit root argument
- a Go or shell-backed regression test under cli/internal/agent that runs the helper with a fake go executable and inspects its arguments

NON-SCOPE
Do not broaden the hook to the full repository, remove -race, raise or remove the timeout, silently ignore unmapped Go paths, or change which staged files Lefthook passes to the command.

PARENT
None; root hook-validation reliability defect discovered during the Niflheim queue drain.

DEPS
None. Related prior hook reliability work is ddx-42a86089; duplicate-hook work is ddx-8a78ee90.

5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run "TestExecutionCleanup_(PreservesLiveFixtureBinaryScratch|ReclaimsDeadFixtureBinaryScratch|PreservesUnownedFixtureBinaryScratch|DefaultPrefixesRequireFixtureOwnerMarker)$" -count=1 passes.
6. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... passes.

description:
PROBLEM
The cleanup allowlist recognizes ddx-fixture-bin-* but not ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*. Adding the missing prefix without ownership evidence would make directory age alone sufficient to delete a live process-owned binary directory. Cleanup must reclaim abandoned directories for both prefixes while preserving any directory still owned by a live process.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:26-46 includes ddx-fixture-bin-* in defaultExecutionCleanupScratchPrefixes but omits ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-*.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:667-681 synthesizes ownership when cleanup.json is absent, while cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:728-755 removes an allowlisted directory after the age threshold when no liveness evidence preserves it.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:189-221 preserves a directory with live PID or lease evidence only when compatible metadata exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Teach execution cleanup to recognize both ddx-fixture-bin-* and ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-* through the internal/scratchowner marker contract. Preserve an old directory while its recorded owner process identity is live; reclaim it only after the owner is dead or conclusively mismatched and the existing minimum-age requirement is satisfied. When process identity cannot be validated safely, preserve the directory and emit a structured uncertain-owner observation. Missing or malformed markers follow the ownership rules from ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93; a prefix alone is never host-global ownership proof. Add ddx-fizeau-testseam-bin-* to defaultExecutionCleanupScratchPrefixes only with the owner-marker preservation path wired, and apply the same ownership and liveness policy to both fixture prefixes.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go and execution_cleanup_test.go

NON-SCOPE
Do not modify fixture_repo.go producers; sibling bead ddx owns marker emission.
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not redesign general host-global scratch trust; ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 own that policy.
Do not reclaim a metadata-less or uncertain-owner host-global directory merely because its name matches a DDx prefix.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
Sibling bead ddx (internal/scratchowner marker contract) must land first so cleanup can read markers.
Sibling bead ddx (fixture producers write marker) must land first so live directories carry owner evidence in tests.
ddx-b2702b9f must land first so both producers use the configured scratch root.
ddx-1eb1ba93 must land first so metadata-marked stale reclamation and host-global ownership rules are established; it already depends on ddx-05e3d16b.

description:
PROBLEM
Running the required cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... gate launches five real Codex provider processes from TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace. In the 2026-07-13 ddx-2502d3c6 attempt, the package test spawned PIDs 225004, 225054, 225173, 225576, and 226111 as __provider-launch ... codex exec; each ran for more than six minutes at about 10-12% CPU. The test package approached its 10-minute timeout, blocking the single queue worker and consuming server-cgroup CPU for a test whose stated concern is only parent-repo Git serialization.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:31-55 builds five production NewRunner(Config{}) instances and labels directive-file paths as model names under the obsolete script route. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:73-89 then calls ExecuteBeadWithConfig concurrently with those production runners. The current service-backed runner resolves the request to Codex, so each directive path is passed to codex exec as -m instead of being consumed by a hermetic script fixture. The test comments at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:35-37 explicitly say agent output is irrelevant. The package previously had to be repaired for the same 600-second budget under ddx-1a0d4d26, but this fixture has regressed into live provider execution.

PROPOSED FIX
- Replace the five production runners in this Git-lock regression with an explicit bounded hermetic AgentRunner fixture that returns the minimal no-changes result needed to reach and validate pre-dispatch serialization.
- Preserve the real temporary Git repository, five concurrent ExecuteBeadWithConfig calls, tracker commits, worktree creation, and HEAD CAS assertions.
- Add a provider-spawn tripwire: real/fake codex, claude, gemini, and provider-launch lookup must fail the test immediately if invoked.
- Audit adjacent direct NewRunner plus Harness=script fixtures reached by the normal internal/agent package gate and migrate any that can invoke live providers to the same hermetic boundary.
- Ensure subprocesses are canceled and reaped on test failure or timeout.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production provider discovery, reduce the concurrency below five, delete the HEAD race assertions, or skip the test. Live provider integration remains build-tagged/explicit integration coverage, not part of the default package gate.

PARENT
None; root regression bead.

DEPS
None.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx consumers need proof that Fizeau v0.15 Execute cancellation does not return while wrapped child or grandchild processes are still alive. Without a focused conformance test, downstream cleanup and lifecycle consumers can incorrectly assume process-tree containment from implementation details instead of the released public Fizeau contract.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/go.mod:5-8 pins github.com/easel/fizeau v0.14.50 and cli/go.sum:88-89 locks that version. cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:196-216 builds the public Execute request, while cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:283-367 consumes final events without proving cancellation waits for wrapped process-tree exit. cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:17-48 is the sole production Fizeau constructor seam and should remain a seam rather than a place for DDx-specific process containment policy. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146 requires released public-boundary conformance before WB-1 consumers proceed.

PROPOSED FIX
After fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c publishes immutable v0.15.0, ensure cli/go.mod and cli/go.sum use github.com/easel/fizeau v0.15.0 exactly if a sibling child has not already landed that pin. Add cli/internal/agent/fizeau_v015_cancellation_contract_test.go using only exported Fizeau APIs. The test must launch a wrapped process that spawns a child or grandchild, cancel Execute, and assert Execute returns only after both PIDs are gone.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement DDx retry, escalation, close, or review policy; adopt Docker portable runtime; delete DDx cleanup shims; add route catalogs or provider probes; select a concrete harness/model/provider; or use Fizeau cost, billing, or route evidence as an execution-policy input. Downstream beads own production consumers after this prerequisite closes. Do not add terminal-cost or portable-plan conformance beyond what is necessary for compilation.

ddx-b8cacbeb.

docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146 and adr:ADR-024.

External blocker fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c must publish v0.15.0 with public typed terminal fields, absent/zero/positive cost presence, wrapped-process-tree containment, and opaque route-neutral portable runtime planning.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-b291b0f6 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as DDx's hidden provider wrapper. During attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, the parent `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, grew a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for 12 minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. This makes the package gate itself create the CPU/memory/orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes that path to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation for the resolved-service path.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83-118` writes each shim as `<ddxBinary> __provider-launch <realBinary>`. Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI and it has no Cobra `__provider-launch` dispatch. Re-executing it starts the test suite again; the recursive process can install shims and launch real providers that escape the original gate process group.
- `cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:25-68` is the actual hidden-command implementation, and exists only in the DDx CLI command graph.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one injectable resolver for the provider-wrapper executable and use it from both service call sites. In package-test builds, install a suite-wide test resolver/guard that refuses to use the current `agent.test` executable as a provider wrapper while leaving direct `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` tests free to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Fail closed with actionable evidence if a test fixture attempts to install a provider shim from a Go test binary. Preserve production PATH shim, `Pdeathsig`, process-group, and real CLI hidden-command behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate or merely increase its timeout.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.
- Scanner injection remains owned by `ddx-02200b1e`; fixture-specific spawn tripwires remain owned by `ddx-26bf19c7`.

PARENT AND DEPS
...[truncated]

- `TestAgentPackageSuite_DoesNotExecTestBinaryAsProviderLauncher` exercises the suite guard and proves no descendant command line matches `agent.test __provider-launch` and no real codex, claude, gemini, opencode, or pi process is launched.
- Existing `TestExecutor_ProviderSpawnSetsPdeathsigAndSetpgid` and cmd-package `TestProviderLaunchExecsProviderInDedicatedProcessGroup` remain green against an explicit DDx CLI/fake binary, proving production parent-death and process-group behavior is preserved.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path that does not exist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifact names instead of current-revision evidence, and the analyzer currently reports nothing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the runtime artifact target resolver into the spechonesty analyzer run. For each Complete/Implemented document mapping row classified as an inspectable runtime artifact target, emit a missing-artifact diagnostic when the target does not resolve, naming the path exactly as written in the mapping row and identifying the requirement and source document. Rows that resolve pass artifact validation and emit nothing. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
Every bead attempt creates a fresh checkout and deletes it on cleanup, so identical sequential work on the same project pays full setup cost each time and discards all local state. Making a workspace survive between beads is only safe if DDx can prove the next bead sees exactly its requested base revision with no residue from the previous bead, and can refuse reuse when it cannot prove that.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:116-149` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare`) creates a linked worktree at a fresh attempt-specific path via `gitOps.WorktreeAdd`, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) unconditionally runs `WorktreeRemove`.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:199-233` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Prepare`) runs a full `git clone` plus `checkout --detach` for every attempt, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) deletes the whole clone with `os.RemoveAll`.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) documents that local-clone is the sandbox-safe default, so the default path is the one paying full clone cost per bead.
- There is no reset/scrub path anywhere in `attempt_backend.go`: because the directory is always new, no code establishes that staged changes, modified tracked files, untracked files, evidence under `.ddx/executions/`, environment-derived credentials, or cleanup metadata written by `WriteExecutionCleanupMetadata` (`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031`) are absent.

PROPOSED FIX
Build on the slot allocator from the sibling bead "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface" (DEPENDS ON that child; do not start until its allocator and config land). Teach both `WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare` and `LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Prepare` to request a slot, and when a healthy slot with a matching repository identity already exists, reset it to the requested base revision instead of recreating it: hard-reset tracked state, scrub staged and modified files, remove untracked files including evidence directories and attempt cleanup metadata, drop environment-derived credential material, and preserve only explicitly allowlisted paths. Verify repository identity before reuse and fall back to a fresh workspace on mismatch. On cleanup, return a healthy slot to the pool; on cleanup failure, surviving descendant processes, or a failed post-reset integrity check, quarantine the slot so it is never reused and emit operator-visible diagnostics. Preserve existing stale-worktree-registration recovery (`isStaleWorktreeRegistrationError`, `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:157-173`) and the existing `KeepOnError` behaviour.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation (sibling child).
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry (sibling child).

PROBLEM
While the managed DDx worker decomposed ddx-29491a0e on 2026-07-13, the preclaim-decompose Codex provider remained live for more than two minutes, but `ddx work status --json` changed to active_work.count=0 and reported no bead_id, phase, or last_activity_at. Operators therefore see an apparently idle worker while queue-critical model work is running.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 constructs the sidecar liveness reporter but explicitly defers emission until a bead is claimed. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without setting a resolving phase or ticking liveness.

PROPOSED FIX
Publish candidate-scoped resolving liveness before dispatching preclaim decomposition, heartbeat it while the provider runs, and include provider-child observations without creating a bead lease. The sidecar status must expose the candidate bead ID, phase=resolving, refreshed last_activity_at, and provider-child metadata before any claim or lease exists.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

1. TestCompleteVerificationMissingRuntimeArtifactEmitsDiagnostic passes: a Complete fixture mapping a requirement to a nonexistent inspectable runtime artifact emits a missing-artifact diagnostic naming the path exactly as written in the mapping row.
2. TestImplementedVerificationMissingRuntimeArtifactEmitsDiagnostic passes: an Implemented fixture mapping a requirement to a nonexistent inspectable runtime artifact emits a missing-artifact diagnostic naming the path exactly as written in the mapping row.
3. TestMissingRuntimeArtifactDoesNotFireForNonRuntimeTargets passes: unresolved evidence targets outside the inspectable runtime artifact classification do not emit the runtime missing-artifact diagnostic.

5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path that does not exist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifact names instead of current-revision evidence, and the analyzer currently reports nothing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend the spechonesty analyzer runtime-artifact validation so each Complete/Implemented Verification mapping row classified as an inspectable runtime artifact target emits a missing-artifact diagnostic when the resolver cannot resolve the target. The diagnostic must name the artifact path exactly as written in the mapping row and must be emitted only for unresolved inspectable runtime artifact targets. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

2. TestImporter_Verify_DetectsDrift exercises the read-back path from Axon target data rather than only comparing in-memory source fixtures.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/... -run 'TestImporter_Verify_DetectsDrift' passes.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires post-migration verification that reads migrated beads back from Axon/Postgres and detects field-level drift. Drift detection should be independently executable from clean round-trip fixture expansion, dry-run behavior, write-path apply mechanics, and CLI routing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer exposes MigrateAxonOptions.Verify at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:38 and calls verifyImportedAxonCorpus from cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:113 after writes. If verifyImportedAxonCorpus or its comparison helpers are absent or shallow, ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify can report success even when stored Axon data differs from the JSONL source corpus.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or complete verifyImportedAxonCorpus and supporting comparison helpers so verification reads back the imported Axon target corpus, compares migrated source beads field-for-field, and returns an error that names the affected bead ID and the drifted field when target data is changed post-import. Keep implementation compatible with existing sample-based verification if a corpus-size threshold already exists; otherwise compare the bounded imported set produced by --limit or the full import.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- CLI flag parsing beyond consuming the Verify option; sibling child owns command UX.
- Core apply/idempotency mechanics except as needed to create verifier fixtures; sibling child owns apply path.
- Dry-run counting/no-mutation semantics; sibling child owns dry-run behavior.
- Clean round-trip fixture breadth for attachment/extras preservation; sibling child owns that proof.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

GOVERNING CONTEXT

title: Implement Axon importer drift verification

acceptance:
1. `TestDecompositionDepthPolicyIsUnified` in `cli/internal/agent/` proves that preclaim intake (`execute_bead_loop.go:2847`), post-attempt recovery (`execute_bead_loop.go:3208`), the queue drain path (`execute_bead_loop.go:520`), and the prompt hint rendered by `executeBeadDynamicStep0Hints` all resolve the same cap value for a given config, including when `agent.triage.max_decomposition_depth` is unset, zero, and explicitly set.
2. `TestDecompositionDepthPolicyIsUnified` also asserts that under the default (unset) policy no code path permits creating a third generated child level: a bead already at the default cap yields no new descendants from any of the four paths.
3. `TestPostAttemptTooLargeNoChanges_UsesQueueDepthNotAttemptPromptDepth` in `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_intake_decompose_test.go:534` is replaced or rewritten so it asserts the unified policy (prompt cap and queue cap agree) instead of preserving conflicting caps; the old assertion that a configured depth of 3 overrides the prompt cap of 2 no longer exists in the tree.
4. `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go` no longer contains an independent depth constant that can disagree with the resolved config value, verified by `TestDecompositionDepthPolicyIsUnified` reading the rendered prompt text for the resolved number.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/... -run 'TestDecompositionDepthPolicyIsUnified|TestPostAttemptTooLargeNoChanges' -count=1` passes.
6. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/...` passes.
7. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes on the final staged tree.
description:
PROBLEM
DDx has two disagreeing decomposition depth caps. Queue triage uses a configurable cap defaulting to three generated levels, while the implementation prompt tells agents there is a hard cap of two. The queue cap wins, so already-narrow beads get another generated layer. In the live Niflheim queue this produced chains such as `niflheim-8c7428de -> niflheim-515a7439 -> niflheim-b476f419 -> niflheim-34c8eb2e/niflheim-6cfc6148` and `niflheim-4093e6df -> niflheim-586e9520 -> niflheim-10932cf3 -> niflheim-e3a5db27/niflheim-e076a89c`, and during a 39-minute observation window one bead closed while open work grew 130 -> 137 and ready work grew 73 -> 77.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/config/types.go:483-501` defines `TriageConfig.MaxDecompositionDepth` and `ResolveMaxDecompositionDepth`, whose `const defaultDepth = 3` is the queue-side cap.
- `cli/internal/config/resolved.go:137` and `cli/internal/config/resolved.go:397-403` surface that value as `ResolvedConfig.MaxDecompositionDepth()`.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2463` declares a separate `executeBeadAutoDecompositionDepthCap = 2`, used at `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2479` only to render a prompt hint. The prompt therefore states a cap the orchestrator does not enforce.
- Consumers read the queue cap independently at `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:520`, `:2847-2848`, and `:3208`, so there is no single resolved policy value.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_intake_decompose_test.go:534-612` (`TestPostAttemptTooLargeNoChanges_UsesQueueDepthNotAttemptPromptDepth`) deliberately pins the disagreement: it asserts a configured depth of 3 overrides the prompt cap of 2 and still creates a child.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one resolved decomposition-depth policy used by preclaim intake, post-attempt recovery, prompt rendering, and configuration. Lower the default to at most two generated child levels. Make `executeBeadDynamicStep0Hints` render the resolved policy value rather than a private constant, and delete `executeBeadAutoDecompositionDepthCap` as an independent cap. All four call sites must resolve the identical number so no path can add a third generated layer under the default policy. Preserve the ability to configure `agent.triage.max_decomposition_depth` explicitly, but reject or clamp nothing silently: the resolved value is what the prompt states.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not prohibit legitimate epic decomposition or independent parallel deliverables.
- Do not weaken acceptance validation or readiness checks.
- Do not change model routing or retry policy except where it currently triggers another decomposition layer.
- Do not rewrite the existing Niflheim tracker.
- Material-scope-reduction gating, at-cap atomic execution, family expansion budget, and telemetry belong to the sibling children of this parent, not here.
- Malformed deterministic fallback children remain owned by `ddx-6ded197d`; preclaim lifecycle process reaping remains owned by `ddx-092f0d34`.

DEPENDENCIES
No deps. This child must land first; the three sibling children depend on the unified policy value it introduces.

description:
PROBLEM
A code-changing execute-bead attempt can bypass required staged hooks and still be accepted. Attempt 20260713T094206-53684645 for ddx-415c8b95 committed with git commit --no-verify after its pre-commit run was interrupted; DDx merged and closed it.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go:160-186 validates gate evidence only when GateRuns is non-empty, while cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1507-1514 calls ValidateAttemptIntegrity without evidence. The validator therefore treats missing evidence as success and does not distinguish implementation-agent bypass commands from orchestrator-owned commits.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the attempt-integrity validator fail closed when a code-changing bead requires a staged lefthook run but meaningful successful evidence is absent. Reject implementation-agent commit commands that use --no-verify. Explicitly retain the scoped exception for DDx-owned checkpoint, tracker-only, landing, and durable-audit commits, which are outside implementation-agent evidence.

- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation_test.go

NON-SCOPE
Do not wire live harness evidence or change execute-bead prompts; ddx-03568f89 owns that integration. Do not rewrite existing execution history or forbid DDx-owned orchestration commits.

ddx-9c3e703b.

title: Verify Axon importer dry-run counts without mutation
work-last-detail: Claude TUI PTY closed before Stop hook; process exit code 1

acceptance:
1. `TestDecompositionFamilyExpansionBudgetStopsQueueGrowth` in `cli/internal/agent/` drives repeated preclaim and post-attempt decomposition rounds against one bead family and asserts the total descendant count never exceeds the configured family-wide budget.
2. The same test asserts that once the budget is reached, each subsequent round produces exactly one stable parked/refusal outcome with a reason and creates zero additional beads — the outcome is identical across rounds rather than cycling between decompose and park.
3. `TestDecompositionEventCarriesFamilyTelemetry` asserts the `triage-decomposed` event body built by `applyPreClaimDecomposition` (`execute_bead_loop.go:6350`) and `decomposerEventBodyForResult` (`recovery_decompose.go:262`) include family size, family depth, split reason, and refusal reason for both an accepted split and a budget refusal.
4. The family expansion budget is configurable under `agent.triage` in `cli/internal/config/types.go` with a documented conservative default, and a config test asserts unset and non-positive values resolve to that default.
5. Existing tests for valid epic decomposition and independent parallel child work remain green.
6. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/... -run 'TestDecompositionFamilyExpansionBudgetStopsQueueGrowth|TestDecompositionEventCarriesFamilyTelemetry' -count=1` passes.
7. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/...` passes.
8. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes on the final staged tree.
description:
PROBLEM
Depth caps alone do not bound queue growth: a bead family can keep widening below the cap because repeated preclaim and post-attempt decisions have no family-wide descendant budget. Operators also cannot distinguish landed progress from queue expansion, because splits and refusals are not reported with family size, depth, or reason. In the live Niflheim queue this showed up as open work growing 130 -> 137 and ready work 73 -> 77 across a 39-minute window with one close.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2847-2848` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3208` bound decomposition by depth only; neither counts existing descendants of the bead family before proposing more children.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6319-6360` (`applyPreClaimDecomposition`) creates children and appends a `triage-decomposed` event unconditionally, so nothing stops repeated rounds from widening the family.
- `cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:246-294` (`appendPreClaimDecomposeEvent` / `decomposerEventBodyForResult`) records child IDs and a fallback reason but not family size, family depth, split reason, or refusal reason — the data an operator needs to see expansion instead of throughput.
- `cli/internal/config/types.go:483-501` exposes only `max_decomposition_depth`; there is no configurable family-wide expansion budget.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a bounded, configurable family-wide descendant/expansion budget alongside the depth cap, resolved through the same policy object. Before any split, count the existing descendants of the bead family; if creating the proposed children would exceed the budget, do not create them — emit exactly one stable parked/refusal outcome with a reason, and keep emitting the same outcome on subsequent rounds rather than cycling between decompose and park. Extend the decomposition event body to carry family size, family depth, split reason, and refusal reason so `ddx` telemetry distinguishes landed progress from queue expansion.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not prohibit legitimate epic decomposition or independent parallel deliverables within budget.
- Do not weaken acceptance validation or readiness checks.
- Do not change model routing or retry policy except where it currently triggers another decomposition layer.
- Do not rewrite the existing Niflheim tracker.
- Depth-policy unification, at-cap atomic execution, and material-scope-reduction gating belong to sibling children.
- Malformed deterministic fallback children remain owned by `ddx-6ded197d`; preclaim lifecycle process reaping remains owned by `ddx-092f0d34`.

DEPENDENCIES
Depends on the sibling child "agent: unify decomposition depth policy across config, intake, recovery, and prompt" (wire its bead ID as a dep at file time); the expansion budget is resolved through the same policy object that child introduces.

However, the DEPENDENCIES section states this bead depends on a sibling child ('agent: unify decomposition depth policy across config, intake, recovery, and prompt') and instructs 'wire its bead ID as a dep at file time' — but no deps field is present in the bead JSON, so that wiring was never done. description:
PROBLEM
After the ddx-29491a0e preclaim decomposer returned on 2026-07-13, an interactive nested `codex --no-alt-screen` process (PID 607041, process group 607041) remained directly under the DDx worker until the operator terminated it. Preclaim providers can therefore leak CPU after successful fallback or other hook exits.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without wrapping the hook in provider-descendant cleanup. Attempt-end descendant reaping in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1150-1163 is never reached because decomposition happens before an implementation attempt exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Establish a preclaim lifecycle process baseline immediately before invoking the decomposition hook and reap every provider descendant introduced by the hook on success, deterministic fallback, error, timeout, and cancellation. Preserve any provider process present in the pre-hook baseline and any process owned by another worker.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:

- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process_test.go and cli/internal/agent/execution_resources_test.go invoke production cleanup paths that can inherit shared roots if call sites are missed.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-24949caf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: Restarting the DDx user service during active supervised work can hang until systemd times out, leaving systemd to SIGKILL server child processes. Live evidence from 2026-07-07 03:05:19 EDT: `ddx server stop` did not return until systemd marked `ddx-server.service` failed with `Result: timeout` and killed leftover git subprocesses, interrupting the Axon worker attempt that was in post-execution handling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: `cli/internal/server/server.go:379-385` cancels the supervisor and then waits on `supervisorDone` with no timeout. Worker cleanup is only reached afterward at `cli/internal/server/server.go:388-395`. The worker shutdown path itself has a bounded wait (`cli/internal/server/workers.go:1696-1703`), but it is unreachable while the supervisor goroutine is stuck in a reconcile/git operation. The installed systemd unit generated from `cli/cmd/server_service.go:26-42` has no explicit stop timeout or ExecStop mitigation, so the default systemd timeout eventually kills the whole cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX: Make server shutdown bounded and ordered so worker cleanup always runs promptly even when supervisor reconciliation is slow or stuck. A good implementation is to cancel the supervisor, wait only a short bounded grace for `supervisorDone`, continue to `supervisorRegistry.Shutdown()` / `workers.Shutdown()` on timeout, and surface/log the supervisor timeout without preventing worker cleanup.

NON-SCOPE: Do not rewrite worker execution semantics, change bead claim/lease policy, or alter unrelated service install behavior.

Parent: none. Dependencies: none.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Add or update a worker-manager shutdown regression so a live managed worker with descendant git/provider subprocesses is reaped through the existing worker shutdown path even when supervisor cancellation is slow.
- `Server.Shutdown()` must not block indefinitely on `supervisorDone`; timeout behavior must return/log a useful error while continuing to close bead hub and stop land coordinators.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

<context-digest>
<principles>Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>

<practices>Integration tests use a real server, git, bead store, DDx worker subprocesses, and a deterministic fake Fizeau fixture · no hosted providers</practices>

Unit and in-process tests do not prove that independently started DDx command processes coordinate through a reachable server and avoid duplicate claims or duplicate landing effects when work is contested.

cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe_integration_test.go:37-88 proves event registration only. cli/internal/server/workers_test.go:875-1007 proves in-process coordinator landing only. No integration test starts real manual and server-managed DDx subprocesses against a real TLS server, git repository, and bead store to prove online contention serializes to exactly one claim and one landing.

PROPOSED FIX
Add TestIntegration_WorkersCoordinateThroughReachableServer under cli/internal/integration/... using a built DDx binary, real TLS server, real git/bead fixture, deterministic script harness, and real DDx subprocesses. Start contested manual and managed workers against the same ready bead, wait for completion, and assert exactly one durable claimant, exactly one landing commit/effect, and no duplicate tracker events for the contested work.

NON-SCOPE
Do not invoke hosted providers, inspect provider descendants from DDx, signal provider processes from DDx, implement routing in DDx, use Docker, or substitute mocks for server/git/bead/landing behavior. Do not cover outage journaling, managed-worker server-death behavior, or Fizeau provider cleanup in this bead.

ddx-635ae251.

ddx-2e49980d: full production coordination wiring must exist before end-to-end proof.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still installs provider-binary PATH shims, exposes a hidden provider-launch wrapper, scans concrete harness process trees, and signals/reaps Fizeau-owned children. Fizeau v0.15 containment work is implemented upstream but not yet published or pinned, so DDx cannot yet delete the safety fallback. Without a dedicated consumer bead, publishing v0.15 would leave this forbidden boundary crossing in DDx indefinitely.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:93-102,116-128,276-297 installs the provider shim and performs route-aware child cleanup around Fizeau Execute.
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:13-56 and 100-179 defines the hidden wrapper contract and concrete provider binary shims.
- cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:12-70 plus provider_launch platform files exposes the direct provider exec boundary.
- cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go:21-40,92-240,242-478 discovers, classifies, signals, and reaps provider children using concrete route/harness facts.
- cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:42-169 plus orphan_harness_reaper_linux.go:22-113 discovers and kills orphan harness processes.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1249-1258 and execute_bead_loop.go:1616-1618 retain attempt-end and liveness integration.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process.go:61-195 and cli/internal/server/workers_reap_unix.go:33-213 mix Fizeau-owned descendants into otherwise DDx-owned attempt/worker cleanup.
- Fizeau containment epic fizeau-c795e7d9 is closed, but release bead fizeau-b9a2037c must publish and prove cancellation/caller-death cleanup before DDx removes the fallback.

PROPOSED FIX
After pinning the compatible Fizeau release, add consumer conformance proving Execute cancellation and caller death terminate every wrapped harness/provider process tree. Delete the PATH shim, hidden provider-launch command/platform implementation, concrete provider binary list, provider-child/orphan-harness census and reapers, route-aware child liveness, attempt-end provider reap, and provider-descendant branches in generic cleanup. DDx retains only cancellation of the context supplied to Fizeau Execute and may supervise/reap DDx-owned worker, attempt, verification, and container processes. No concrete returned route fact may authorize a signal.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken DDx-owned worker/attempt/container cleanup, move bead/worktree/verification/landing ownership to Fizeau, parse terminal text, or implement the typed outcome adapter owned by ddx-66a8883f.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c publishes the process-tree containment contract and is the structured external blocker. fizeau#fizeau-c795e7d9 supplies the already-landed implementation.

description:
PROBLEM
Existing agent tests intentionally create corrupted Git configuration to prove execute-bead repair behavior, but those fixtures must never mutate the real repository running the tests. The two affected tests must keep their intended assertions while operating only inside dedicated fixture repositories.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:1244-1286 deliberately sets `core.bare=true` in a script-harness fixture. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_env_isolation_test.go:181-237 asserts a separate contamination case does not affect the primary checkout. The observed full-hook run of `go test -short -race ./internal/agent` nevertheless rewrote `/home/erik/Projects/ddx/.git/config` at 2026-07-17 09:41 with `core.bare=true` and test user values, which means these fixture paths can still reach shared config outside their intended sandbox.

PROPOSED FIX
Refactor TestExecuteBeadWorkerCannotMutatePrimaryGitConfig and TestWorkRepairsCoreBareAndContinuesSameCandidate setup to create and use dedicated temporary repositories/config scopes for all intentional Git corruption and repair assertions. Snapshot the invoking repository configuration before fixture execution where practical, assert the fixture repository still observes and repairs its own `core.bare=true` state, and make the tests fail during setup if they cannot prove they are targeting private fixture config.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken the existing core.bare/core.worktree repair behavior, remove execute-bead config isolation, alter user project Git configuration, or change DDx/Fizeau routing. This child only changes the existing core.bare repair/contamination fixtures and their focused assertions; stale index-lock recovery is ddx-3f156500 and main-git lock safety is ddx-1c8d9319. Parent bead: ddx-8b22914e. Deps: none; independent defect discovered while validating ddx-3f156500.

acceptance:
1. TestExecuteBeadLoop_RepeatedBestEffortReadinessErrorsDoNotStopDrain creates more than DefaultPreClaimWarnRepeatThreshold ready beads whose pre-claim hook returns the same nonfatal intake error; it proves all beads execute/close, Run has no terminal OperatorAttention, and a durable non-terminal operator-attention event is emitted exactly once.
2. TestPreClaimWarnSameFingerprintEscalatesAfterThreshold or its successor still proves a claim-blocking system_unready policy stops before the threshold bead.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "Test(ExecuteBeadLoop_RepeatedBestEffortReadinessErrorsDoNotStopDrain|PreClaimWarnSameFingerprintEscalatesAfterThreshold)" -count=1 passes.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
A DDx watch worker exits after five distinct beads when the best-effort readiness hook repeatedly returns system_unready, even though each failure is explicitly logged as continuing and the worker can still claim and execute beads. This converts an advisory Fizeau readiness outage into a queue-wide drain stop.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3010-3058 logs intakeErr as "check unavailable ... (continuing)" but passes it to appendPreClaimWarn. execute_bead_loop.go:1961-1984 makes the fifth matching warning set OperatorAttention and terminate Run. The observed watch run exited after ddx-029c1dde, ddx-744b0996, ddx-b0de0d36, and ddx-8c8675ba with preclaim_warn_repeated while all failures were non-blocking readiness-route JSON errors.

PROPOSED FIX
For fail-open best-effort readiness intake errors, retain durable warning/operator-attention observability but do not return Stop from watch/drain execution. Keep terminal behavior for claim-blocking readiness policy, project corruption, and other genuine safety stops. Add focused regression proof using a repeated intakeErr across more than DefaultPreClaimWarnRepeatThreshold beads that confirms the worker completes the available queue and records non-terminal attention.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change Fizeau routing, harness selection, failure-class vocabulary, readiness policy when configured blocking, or bead execution escalation.
